sentences.zh: 李渤，字浚之，後魏橫野將軍申國公發之後。

translations.literal: Li Bo, styled Junzhi, was a descendant of Fa, Prince of Shen and general of the Wild Field Army of the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bo, whose courtesy name was Junzhi, traced his line to Fa, Prince of Shen and a general of the Wild Field Army under the Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖玄珪，衛尉寺主簿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan'gui was a clerk in the Court of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan'gui served as a clerk in the Court of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 父鈞，殿中侍御史，以母喪不時舉，流於施州。

translations.literal: His father Jun was a palace censor; for failing to observe the mourning period for his mother's death in timely fashion, he was exiled to Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun had been a palace censor but was banished to Shizhou for not completing the prescribed mourning for his mother on time.

sentences.zh: 渤恥其家汙，堅苦不仕；

translations.literal: Bo was ashamed of his family's disgrace and resolutely endured hardship without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of his family's stain, Bo endured hardship and steadfastly refused to enter government service.

sentences.zh: 勵誌於文學，不從科舉，隱於嵩山，以讀書業文為事。

translations.literal: He set his will on literary study, did not pursue the civil service examinations, lived in seclusion on Mount Song, and made reading and writing his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to letters, avoided the examination route, withdrew to Mount Song, and made reading and composition his life's work.

sentences.zh: 元和初，戶部侍郎鹽鐵轉運使李巽、諫議大夫韋況更薦之，以山人征為左拾遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe reign, Li Xun, Vice Minister of Revenue and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, and Remonstrance Grandee Wei Kuang both recommended him again, and he was summoned as a Recluse Scholar to the post of Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe, Li Xun, vice minister of revenue and salt-and-iron transport commissioner, and Remonstrance Grandee Wei Kuang recommended him anew, and the court summoned him from recluse status to serve as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 渤托疾不赴，遂家東都。

translations.literal: Bo pleaded illness and did not go; he then made his home in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bo pleaded illness and declined the appointment, settling instead in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 朝廷政有得失，附章疏陳論。

translations.literal: Whenever the court's policies had gains or losses, he attached memorials setting forth his views.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw merit or fault in court policy, he submitted memorials laying out his views.

sentences.zh: 又撰《禦戎新錄》二十卷，表獻之。

translations.literal: He also compiled twenty juan of New Records on Frontier Defense and presented them by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled twenty juan of New Records on Frontier Defense and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 九年，以著作郎征之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned as Master of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the reign he was summoned to serve as Master of Writings.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「特降新恩，用清舊議。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "We specially bestow a new favor to clear away old objections."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "We hereby grant a special favor to set aside the old objections."

sentences.zh: 渤於是赴官。

translations.literal: Bo thereupon took up the office.
translations.idiomatic: Bo then accepted the post and took up office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷右補闕。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Right Supplements-the-Omissions.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he was promoted to Right Supplements-the-Omissions.

sentences.zh: 連上章疏忤旨，改丹王府諮議參軍，分司東都。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials that offended the imperial will and was changed to Adviser-in-Attendance of the Prince of Dan's household, with a detached assignment in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After a string of memorials that ran against the emperor's wishes, he was reassigned as adviser to the Prince of Dan's household and given a detached post in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷贊善大夫，依前分司。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent, retaining his former detached assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent while keeping the same detached assignment.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遣人上疏論時政，凡五事：一禮樂，二食貨，三刑政，四議都，五辯讎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he sent someone to submit a memorial discussing current affairs in five matters: first ritual and music, second food and goods, third punishments and government, fourth deliberation on the capital, fifth distinguishing enmity.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he had a memorial delivered on current affairs covering five topics: ritual and music, food and goods, punishments and administration, deliberation on the capital, and distinguishing enmities.

sentences.zh: 渤以散秩在東都，以上章疏為己任，前後四十五封。

translations.literal: Bo, holding a loose rank in the Eastern Capital, took submitting memorials as his duty and did so forty-five times in all.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held only a nominal post in the Eastern Capital, Bo made memorial-writing his duty and sent forth forty-five in all.

sentences.zh: 再遷為庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director in the Bureau of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to vice director in the Bureau of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 時皇甫镈作相，剝下希旨。

translations.literal: At the time Huangfu Bo served as chief minister, stripping the people below to please the ruler's intent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huangfu Bo was chief minister and squeezed the populace to curry favor with the throne.

sentences.zh: 會澤潞節度使郗士美卒，渤充吊祭使，路次陜西。

translations.literal: When Zelu Military Commissioner Xi Shimei died, Bo served as condolence envoy and passed through Shaanxi on the route.
translations.idiomatic: When Zelu military commissioner Xi Shimei died, Bo was appointed condolence envoy and traveled through Shaanxi on the way.

sentences.zh: 渤上疏曰：「臣出使經行，歷求利病。

translations.literal: Bo submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant, on mission and traveling the route, has everywhere sought benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Bo memorialized: "On this mission Your Servant has traveled the route and everywhere sought out what helps and what harms the realm.

sentences.zh: 竊知渭南縣長源鄉本有四百戶，今才一百余戶；

translations.literal: I have learned in private that Changyuan township in Weinan County originally had four hundred households, but now has only a little more than one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: I have found that Changyuan township in Weinan County once had four hundred households but now has barely more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 闃鄉縣本有三千戶；

translations.literal: Quxiang County originally had three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Quxiang County once had three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 今才有一千戶，其他州縣大約相似。

translations.literal: Now it has only one thousand households; other prefectures and counties are roughly similar.
translations.idiomatic: Today it has only a thousand, and other prefectures and counties are much the same.

sentences.zh: 訪尋積弊，始自均攤逃戶。

translations.literal: Inquiring and tracing accumulated abuses, they begin with equal apportionment of tax burdens onto fleeing households.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the accumulated abuses, I find they begin with spreading the tax burden of fleeing households onto those who remain.

sentences.zh: 凡十家之內，大半逃亡，亦須五家攤稅。

translations.literal: Within every ten households, the greater part have fled, yet five households must still bear apportioned taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In a group of ten households, most may have fled, yet the tax of all ten must still be spread across the five who remain.

sentences.zh: 似投石井中，非到底不止。

translations.literal: It is like casting a stone into a well—it does not stop until it reaches the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: It is like dropping a stone down a well: it will not stop until it hits bottom.

sentences.zh: 攤逃之弊，苛虐如斯，此皆聚斂之臣剝下媚上，唯思竭澤，不慮無魚。

translations.literal: The abuse of apportioning fleeing households' taxes is harsh and cruel to this degree; all these are revenue-gathering ministers who strip those below to flatter those above, thinking only to drain the marsh and not considering that there will be no fish.
translations.idiomatic: The abuse of spreading tax onto fugitive households is cruelty of this order—ministers obsessed with revenue who strip the people to please their superiors, draining the pond without thinking that no fish will be left.

sentences.zh: 乞降詔書，絕攤逃之弊。

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued to end the abuse of apportioning fleeing households' taxes.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that an edict be issued to abolish the practice of spreading fugitive households' taxes onto others.

sentences.zh: 其逃亡戶以其家產錢數為定，征有所欠，乞降特恩免之。

translations.literal: For fleeing households, let the amount of their household property in cash be fixed; for any shortfall in collection, I beg a special grace to remit it.
translations.idiomatic: For households that have fled, fix their liability by the cash value of their property, and for any shortfall in collection I beg a special grace to forgive it.

sentences.zh: 計不數年，人必歸於農矣。

translations.literal: I calculate that within a few years people will surely return to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years, I believe, people will surely return to the land.

sentences.zh: 夫農者，國之本，本立然後可以議太平。

translations.literal: Agriculture is the foundation of the state; only when the foundation is established can one discuss great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Agriculture is the foundation of the state; only when that foundation stands firm can one speak of lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 若不由茲，而雲太平者，謬矣。」

translations.literal: If one does not proceed by this and yet speaks of great peace, it is erroneous."
translations.idiomatic: To speak of peace without proceeding from this is simply wrong."

sentences.zh: 又言道途不修，驛馬多死。

translations.literal: He also spoke of roads not being repaired and many relay horses dying.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that the roads were neglected and many relay horses were dying.

sentences.zh: 憲宗覽疏驚異，即以飛龍馬數百匹，付畿內諸驛。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong, reading the memorial, was startled; he immediately gave several hundred Flying Dragon horses to the relay stations within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong read the memorial with astonishment and at once supplied several hundred Flying Dragon horses to the relay stations of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 渤既以草疏切直，大忤宰相，乃謝病東歸。

translations.literal: Bo, having drafted a memorial that was cutting and direct, greatly offended the chief minister and thereupon pleaded illness and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Because his draft memorial had been blunt and forthright, Bo had deeply offended the chief minister and pleaded illness to return to the east.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，召為考功員外郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Bo was summoned as Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Bo was recalled as vice director in the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 十一月，定京官考，不避權幸，皆行升黜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he fixed the evaluations of capital officials, not avoiding the powerful and favored, and carried out promotions and demotions for all.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he conducted the capital officials' evaluations without sparing the powerful and favored, promoting and demoting as merit required.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：宰臣蕭俛、段文昌、崔植，是陛下君臨之初，用為輔弼，安危理亂，決在此時。

translations.literal: The memorial said: The chief ministers Xiao Xian, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Zhi were appointed as assistants at the beginning of Your Majesty's rule over the realm; whether the state is secure or in peril, well governed or in disorder, is decided at this moment.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial read: Chief ministers Xiao Xian, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Zhi were appointed as your assistants when you first took the throne; whether the state stands secure or in peril, well governed or in disorder, is decided at this moment.

sentences.zh: 況陛下思天下和平，敬大臣禮切，固未有昵比左右、侈滿自賢之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty thinks of peace under Heaven and honors great ministers with earnest courtesy; you truly have no heart to favor those at your side or to be arrogant and self-admiring.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty seeks peace under Heaven and honors great ministers with earnest courtesy; you truly have no wish to favor those at your side or to grow arrogant and self-admiring.

sentences.zh: 而宰相之權，宰相之事，陛下一以付之，實君義臣行，千載一遇之時也。

translations.literal: Yet the authority of the chancellor and the affairs of the chancellor Your Majesty has entirely entrusted to them; this is truly a time when ruler and subject fulfill their roles, a meeting once in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have entrusted chancellors with chancellors' authority and chancellors' affairs; this is truly a moment when ruler and subject fulfill their proper roles—a meeting once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 此時若失，他更無時。

translations.literal: If this moment is lost, there will be no other time.
translations.idiomatic: If this moment is lost, there will be no other.

sentences.zh: 而俛等上不能推至公，申炯誡，陳先王道德，以沃君心；

translations.literal: Yet Xian and the others, above, cannot promote utmost fairness, set forth bright admonitions, and expound the moral virtue of former kings to nourish the ruler's heart;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xian and the others cannot, on the one hand, promote utmost fairness, set forth bright admonitions, and expound the moral virtue of former kings to nourish your heart;

sentences.zh: 又不能正色匪躬，振舉舊法，復百司之本，俾教化大立。

translations.literal: nor, below, can they maintain a stern countenance and devote themselves, revive the old laws, restore the foundations of the hundred offices, and cause great instruction and transformation to be established.
translations.idiomatic: nor can they, on the other hand, maintain a stern countenance and devote themselves wholeheartedly, revive the old laws, restore the foundations of the hundred offices, and establish instruction and transformation on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 臣聞政之興廢，在於賞罰。

translations.literal: This subject has heard that whether government rises or falls depends on rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that whether government flourishes or fails depends on rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 俛等作相已來，未聞獎一人德義，舉守官奉公者，使天下在官之徒有所激勸；

translations.literal: Since Xian and the others became chancellors, one has not heard of rewarding a single man of virtue and righteousness or promoting one who keeps his office and serves the public, so that those in office throughout the realm might be stirred to emulation;
translations.idiomatic: Since Xian and the others became chancellors, one has not heard of a single reward for virtue and righteousness or promotion of an official who keeps his post and serves the public, so that those in office throughout the realm might be stirred to emulation;

sentences.zh: 又不聞黜一人職事不理、持祿養驕者，使屍祿之徒有所懼。

translations.literal: nor has one heard of dismissing a single man whose duties were neglected and who held salary while nurturing arrogance, so that those who occupy posts in name only might feel fear.
translations.idiomatic: nor has one heard of a single dismissal of an official who neglected his duties and held salary while nurturing arrogance, so that those who occupy posts in name only might feel fear.

sentences.zh: 如此，則刑法不立矣！

translations.literal: If it is like this, then the penal laws are not established!
translations.idiomatic: If this is so, then the penal laws cannot stand!

sentences.zh: 邪正莫辯，混然無章，教化不行，賞罰之設，天下之事，復何望哉！

translations.literal: The wicked and the upright cannot be distinguished; all is confused and without order; instruction and transformation are not carried out—of the institution of rewards and punishments and affairs under Heaven, what can one still hope for!
translations.idiomatic: Wicked and upright cannot be distinguished; all is confused and without order; instruction and transformation are not carried out—what can one still hope for from rewards and punishments and affairs under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 一昨陛下遊幸驪山，宰相、翰林學士是陛下股肱心腹，宜皆知之。

translations.literal: Just yesterday Your Majesty toured Mount Li; the chancellors and Hanlin academicians are Your Majesty's arms, legs, heart, and belly—they ought all to have known of it.
translations.idiomatic: Just yesterday Your Majesty toured Mount Li; the chancellors and Hanlin academicians are your closest ministers—they ought all to have known of it.

sentences.zh: 蕭俛等不能先事未形，忘軀懇諫，而使陛下有忽諫之名流於史冊，是陷君於過也。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian and the others could not, before the matter had taken shape, forget their bodies and remonstrate earnestly, and thereby caused Your Majesty to have the name of disregarding remonstrance flow into the historical records—this is entangling the ruler in fault.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian and the others could not, before the matter had taken shape, forget themselves and remonstrate earnestly, and thereby left Your Majesty with the name of disregarding remonstrance in the historical records—this is entangling the ruler in fault.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「所謂大臣者，以道事君，不可則止。」

translations.literal: Confucius said, "What is called a great minister is one who serves the ruler by the Way; if it cannot be done, then he stops."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "What is called a great minister is one who serves the ruler by the Way; if it cannot be done, then he stops."

sentences.zh: 若俛等言行計從，不當如是。

translations.literal: If Xian and the others' words and deeds were followed in plan, they ought not to be like this.
translations.idiomatic: If Xian and the others' words and plans were being followed, they ought not to act like this.

sentences.zh: 若言不行，計不從，須奉身速退，不宜屍素於化源。

translations.literal: If their words are not carried out and their plans are not followed, they must withdraw their persons and retire quickly; they ought not to occupy posts in name only at the source of transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If their words are not carried out and their plans are not followed, they must withdraw and retire quickly; they ought not to occupy posts in name only at the source of transformation.

sentences.zh: 進退戾也，何所避辭？

translations.literal: Their advance and retreat are perverse—what is there to avoid in speech?
translations.idiomatic: Their advance and retreat are perverse—what excuse can they offer?

sentences.zh: 其蕭亻免、段文昌、崔植三人並翰林學士杜元穎等，並請考中下。

translations.literal: As for Xiao Xian, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Zhi, the three men, together with Hanlin Academician Du Yuanying and others, all are requested to receive middle-lower evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Zhi, together with Hanlin Academician Du Yuanying and others, should all receive middle-lower evaluations.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李絳、左散騎常侍張惟素、右散騎常侍李益等諫幸驪山，鄭覃等諫畋遊，是皆恐陛下行幸不息，恣情無度；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Jiao, Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse Zhang Weisu, Right Regular Attendant of the Palace Horse Li Yi, and others remonstrated against the tour of Mount Li; Zheng Tan and others remonstrated against hunting excursions—all because they feared Your Majesty's tours would not cease and your feelings would be indulged without limit;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Jiao, Left Regular Attendant Zhang Weisu, Right Regular Attendant Li Yi, and others remonstrated against the tour of Mount Li; Zheng Tan and others remonstrated against hunting excursions—all because they feared Your Majesty's tours would not cease and your feelings would be indulged without limit;

sentences.zh: 又恐馬有銜蹶不測之變，風寒生疾之憂，急奏無所詣，國璽委於婦人中幸之手。

translations.literal: they also feared unforeseen mishaps of horses stumbling in the bit, the worry of illness arising from wind and cold, urgent memorials having nowhere to reach, and the imperial seal entrusted to the hands of women and favored attendants.
translations.idiomatic: they also feared unforeseen mishaps of horses stumbling in the bit, illness arising from wind and cold, urgent memorials having nowhere to reach, and the imperial seal entrusted to the hands of women and favored attendants.

sentences.zh: 絳等能率御史諫官論列於朝，有懇激事君之體。

translations.literal: Jiao and the others were able to lead censorial remonstrance officials in setting forth arguments at court, showing the earnest and impassioned manner of serving the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao and the others were able to lead censorial remonstrance officials in setting forth arguments at court, showing the earnest and impassioned manner of serving the ruler.

sentences.zh: 其李絳、張惟素、李益三人，伏請賜上下考外，特與遷官，以彰陛下優忠賞諫之美。

translations.literal: As for Li Jiao, Zhang Weisu, and Li Yi, the three men, this subject humbly requests that, in addition to granting upper-lower evaluations, they be specially promoted in office, to display Your Majesty's excellence in honoring loyalty and rewarding remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiao, Zhang Weisu, and Li Yi should, in addition to receiving upper-lower evaluations, be specially promoted in office, to display Your Majesty's excellence in honoring loyalty and rewarding remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 其崔元略冠供奉之首，合考上下；

translations.literal: As for Cui Yuanlue, who heads the Palace Attendance Service, he ought to receive upper-lower evaluation;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanlue, who heads the Palace Attendance Service, ought to receive upper-lower evaluation;

sentences.zh: 緣與於翚上下考，於翚以犯贓處死，準令須降，請賜考中中。

translations.literal: because he shared upper-lower evaluation with Yu Hui, and Yu Hui was executed for the crime of corruption; according to the statute the grade must be lowered—please grant middle-middle evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: because he shared upper-lower evaluation with Yu Hui, who was executed for corruption; according to statute the grade must be lowered—please grant middle-middle evaluation.

sentences.zh: 大理卿許季同，任使於翚、韋道沖、韋正牧，皆以犯贓，或左降，或處死，合考中下；

translations.literal: Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Jitong, in appointing Yu Hui, Wei Daochong, and Wei Zhengmu, all of whom committed corruption and were either demoted or executed, ought to receive middle-lower evaluation;
translations.idiomatic: Chief Judge Xu Jitong, in appointing Yu Hui, Wei Daochong, and Wei Zhengmu—all of whom committed corruption and were either demoted or executed—ought to receive middle-lower evaluation;

sentences.zh: 然頃者陷劉辟之亂，棄家歸朝，忠節明著，今宜以功補過，請賜考中中。

translations.literal: yet recently, trapped in Liu Pi's rebellion, he abandoned his household and returned to court; his loyalty and integrity were clearly shown—now merit should offset fault; please grant middle-middle evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: yet recently, trapped in Liu Pi's rebellion, he abandoned his household and returned to court, his loyalty and integrity clearly shown—merit should now offset fault; please grant middle-middle evaluation.

sentences.zh: 少府監裴通，職事修舉，合考中上；

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Storehouses Pei Tong, whose duties were well performed, ought to receive middle-upper evaluation;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Storehouses Pei Tong, whose duties were well performed, ought to receive middle-upper evaluation;

sentences.zh: 以其請追封所生母而舍嫡母，是明罔於君，幽欺其先，請考中下。

translations.literal: because he requested posthumous enfeoffment for his birth mother while setting aside his legal mother—this is openly deceiving the ruler and secretly deceiving his ancestors—please grant middle-lower evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: because he requested posthumous enfeoffment for his birth mother while setting aside his legal mother—openly deceiving the ruler and secretly deceiving his ancestors—please grant middle-lower evaluation.

sentences.zh: 伏以昔在宰夫入寢，擅飲師曠、李調。

translations.literal: This subject humbly notes that in antiquity, when a cook entered the sleeping chamber and presumptuously drank with Shi Kuang and Li Diao,
translations.idiomatic: I humbly note that in antiquity, when a cook entered the sleeping chamber and presumptuously drank with Shi Kuang and Li Diao,

sentences.zh: 今愚臣守官，請書宰相學士中下考。

translations.literal: today this foolish subject, keeping his office, requests that the chancellors and academicians be recorded with middle-lower evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: today I, keeping my office, request that the chancellors and academicians be recorded with middle-lower evaluations.

sentences.zh: 上愛聖運，下振頹綱，故臣懼不言之為罪，不懼言之為罪也。

translations.literal: Above, loving the sage fortune; below, reviving the collapsed norms—therefore this subject fears that not speaking would be a crime, and does not fear that speaking would be a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Loving the sage fortune above and reviving collapsed norms below—I fear that not speaking would be a crime, and do not fear that speaking would be a crime.

sentences.zh: 其三品官考，伏緣限在今月內進，輒先具如前。

translations.literal: As for evaluations of third-rank officials, because the deadline falls within this month, this subject ventures to set them forth first as above.
translations.idiomatic: Because evaluations of third-rank officials are due within this month, I venture to set them forth first as above.

sentences.zh: 其四品以下官，續具條疏聞奏。

translations.literal: For officials of fourth rank and below, a detailed memorial will be submitted in continuation.
translations.idiomatic: For officials of fourth rank and below, a detailed memorial will be submitted in continuation.

sentences.zh: 狀入，留中不下。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and was kept within without being issued.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne but was held within and never issued.

sentences.zh: 議者以宰輔曠官，自宜上疏論列，而渤越職釣名，非盡事君之道。

translations.literal: Discussants held that the chief ministers were neglecting their offices and that one should naturally submit memorials setting this forth, but that Bo overstepped his duties to fish for reputation and did not fully follow the way of serving one's lord.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that the chief ministers were neglecting duty and that memorials ought to say so—but that Bo had overstepped his role to court fame and had not fully observed the way of serving one's sovereign.

sentences.zh: 未幾，渤以墜馬傷足，請告，會魏博節度使田弘正表渤為副使。

translations.literal: Before long Bo, having fallen from a horse and injured his foot, requested leave; it happened that Weibo Military Commissioner Tian Hongzheng memorialized recommending Bo as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Bo fell from his horse and injured his foot and requested leave; at the same time Weibo military commissioner Tian Hongzheng memorialized recommending Bo as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 杜元穎奏曰：「渤賣直沽名，動多狂躁。

translations.literal: Du Yuanying memorialized, saying: "Bo sells forthrightness to buy reputation and is often rash and impetuous in his actions.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuanying memorialized: "Bo trades on blunt honesty to buy a reputation and is habitually rash and impetuous.

sentences.zh: 聖恩矜貸，且使居官。

translations.literal: The sage grace has shown pity and leniency, yet he is still allowed to hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's grace has spared him and allowed him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 而幹進多端，外交方鎮，遠求奏請，不能自安。

translations.literal: Yet he schemes advancement by many means, maintains external ties with regional commands, and seeks distant memorial recommendations, unable to rest content.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he schemes for advancement by every means, cultivates ties with the regional commands, and seeks distant appointments by memorial—he cannot rest content at court.

sentences.zh: 久留在朝，轉恐生事。」

translations.literal: If he remains long at court, I fear he will in turn cause trouble."
translations.idiomatic: If he stays long at court, I fear he will only cause trouble."

sentences.zh: 乃出為虔州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then sent out as prefect of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon sent out to serve as prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 渤至州，奏還鄰境信州所移兩稅錢二百萬，免稅米二萬斛，減所由一千六百人。

translations.literal: When Bo reached the prefecture, he memorialized to return two million cash in dual-tax monies transferred from neighboring Xinzhou, to remit twenty thousand bushels of tax grain, and to reduce subordinates by sixteen hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the prefecture, Bo memorialized to return two million cash in dual-tax funds shifted from neighboring Xinzhou, to remit twenty thousand bushels of tax grain, and to cut sixteen hundred subordinate staff.

sentences.zh: 觀察使以其事上聞。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner reported his actions to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The observation commissioner reported these measures to the throne.

sentences.zh: 未滿歲，遷江州刺史。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed, he was transferred to prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year was out he was transferred to prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 張平叔判度支，奏征久遠逋懸，渤在州上疏曰：「伏奉詔敕，雲度支使所奏，令臣設計征填當州貞元二年逃戶所欠錢四千四百一十貫。

translations.literal: Zhang Pingshu oversaw the Department of Public Works and memorialized to collect long-standing arrears; Bo, in the prefecture, submitted a memorial saying: "I have received the edict stating that the revenue commissioner memorialized ordering your servant to devise means to collect and make up the four thousand four hundred and ten strings owed by fleeing households of the second year of Zhenyuan in this prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pingshu, overseeing the Department of Public Works, memorialized to collect long-overdue arrears; from Jiangzhou Bo wrote: "I have received the edict citing the revenue commissioner's request that I devise means to collect the four thousand four hundred and ten strings owed by households that fled in the second year of Zhenyuan in this prefecture.

sentences.zh: 臣當州管田二千一百九十七頃，今已旱死一千九百頃有余，若更勒徇度支使所為，必懼史官書陛下於大旱中征三十六年前逋懸。

translations.literal: Your servant's prefecture administers two thousand one hundred and ninety-seven qing of fields; more than one thousand nine hundred qing have now died from drought; if I further compel compliance with what the revenue commissioner has done, I must fear the historians will record that Your Majesty collected thirty-six-year-old arrears amid great drought.
translations.idiomatic: This prefecture administers two thousand one hundred ninety-seven qing of fields, of which more than nineteen hundred have already been lost to drought; if I were forced to carry out the revenue commissioner's order, I fear the historians will record that Your Majesty collected arrears thirty-six years old in the midst of great drought.

sentences.zh: 臣任刺史，罪無所逃。

translations.literal: Your servant holds the post of prefect; guilt has nowhere to flee.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect I cannot escape blame.

sentences.zh: 臣既上不副聖情，下不忍鞭笞黎庶，不敢輕持符印，特乞放臣歸田。」

translations.literal: Your servant, failing above to match the sage intent and below unable to bear flogging the common people, dares not lightly hold the seal and tally and specially begs to be released to return to the fields."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot meet Your Majesty's intent above, nor bear to flog the people below; I dare not lightly keep my seal of office and beg to be released to return to my fields."

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「江州所奏，實為懇誠。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued, saying: "What Jiangzhou has memorialized is truly earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: The court then issued an edict: "Jiangzhou's memorial is truly earnest and sincere.

sentences.zh: 若不蠲容，必難存濟。

translations.literal: If we do not remit and tolerate, survival will surely be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Without remission the people cannot survive.

sentences.zh: 所訴逋欠並放。」

translations.literal: All the arrears appealed are remitted."
translations.idiomatic: All the arrears in question were forgiven."

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，入為職方郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing he entered the capital as Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing he was recalled to the capital as director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 敬宗沖年即位，坐朝常晚。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong took the throne in his youth and often held court late.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong came to the throne young and habitually held court late.

sentences.zh: 一日入閣，久不坐，群臣候立紫宸門外，有耆年衰病者，幾將頓仆。

translations.literal: One day he entered the inner court but long did not take his seat; the officials waited standing outside the Gate of Purple Felicity, and among them were elderly men weakened by illness who nearly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: One day he entered the inner court but long delayed taking his seat; officials waited outside the Gate of Purple Felicity, and some elderly men, frail with age and illness, nearly collapsed where they stood.

sentences.zh: 渤出次白宰相曰：「昨日拜疏陳論，今坐益晚，是諫官不能回人主之意，渤之罪也。

translations.literal: Bo stepped out and told the chief minister in plain words: "Yesterday I submitted a memorial setting forth my views; today the session is even later—this is the remonstrance official's failure to turn back the ruler's intent; it is Bo's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Bo stepped out and told the chief minister plainly: "Yesterday I submitted a memorial on this matter; today court is even later—the remonstrance official has failed to move the sovereign's mind, and that is my fault.

sentences.zh: 請先出閣，待罪於金吾仗。」

translations.literal: I beg to leave the inner court first and await punishment at the Golden Crow guard post."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to withdraw from court first and await punishment at the Golden Crow guard post."

sentences.zh: 語次喚仗，乃止。

translations.literal: In the midst of his words the guard was summoned, and he then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Even as he spoke the guard was summoned, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 渤又以左右常侍，職參觀諷，而循默無言，論之曰：「若設官不責其事，不如罷之，以省經費。

translations.literal: Bo also addressed the Left and Right Attendants-in-Ordinary, whose duty is to participate in observation and admonition yet who followed custom in silence without speaking, criticizing them: "If one establishes offices without charging them with their duties, it would be better to abolish them to save expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Bo also took the Left and Right Attendants-in-Ordinary to task—their duty was to observe and admonish, yet they kept silent—and said: "If offices are created but no duty is required of them, abolish them and save the expense.

sentences.zh: 茍未能罷，則請責職業。」

translations.literal: If they cannot be abolished, then I beg that their professional duties be required."
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot be abolished, then hold them to their duties."

sentences.zh: 渤充理匭使，奏曰：「事之大者聞奏，次申中書門下，次移諸司。

translations.literal: Bo served as commissioner for the Petition Box and memorialized, saying: "Matters of great weight are heard and reported to the throne; next they are referred to the Secretariat and Chancellery; next they are transferred to the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: As commissioner for the Petition Box, Bo memorialized: "Major matters are reported directly to the throne; lesser ones go first to the Secretariat and Chancellery, then to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 諸司處理不當，再來投匭，即具事奏聞。

translations.literal: When the various bureaus handle matters improperly, if one comes again to cast into the box, the matter is then set forth in full and reported to the court.
translations.idiomatic: If the offices mishandle a case and the petitioner returns to the box, the matter should be reported in full to the throne.

sentences.zh: 如妄訴無理，本罪外加一等。

translations.literal: If one makes a false appeal without reason, one degree is added to the original offense.
translations.idiomatic: False or groundless appeals should receive one degree of punishment beyond the underlying offense.

sentences.zh: 準敕告密人付金吾留身待進止。

translations.literal: According to the edict, informers are handed to the Golden Crow to detain the body awaiting imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: By edict, informers are handed to the Golden Crow guard to be detained pending the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 今欲留身後牒臺府，冀止絕兇人。」

translations.literal: Now I wish, after detaining the body, to send a dispatch to the censorate and prefectural offices, hoping to stop and cut off violent men."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that after detention a dispatch go to the censorate and prefectural offices, in hope of deterring malicious accusers."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 長慶、寶歷中，政出多門，事歸邪幸。

translations.literal: During Changqing and Baoli, government issued from many gates and affairs fell to wicked favorites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing and Baoli reigns power leaked through many hands and affairs fell to corrupt favorites.

sentences.zh: 渤不顧忠難，章疏論列，曾無虛日。

translations.literal: Bo, heedless of loyal hardship, set forth his views in memorial after memorial, never a day without.
translations.idiomatic: Bo, heedless of the cost to himself, submitted memorial after memorial—not a day passed without one.

sentences.zh: 帝雖昏縱，亦為之感悟。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was muddled and dissolute, he was also moved to awareness by this.
translations.idiomatic: Even the muddled and dissolute emperor was moved by his persistence.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中，面賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and in person was bestowed gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and personally granted the gold-and-purple insignia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年，改元大赦。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli the reign title was changed and a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli the reign title was changed and a great amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄠縣令崔發聞門外喧鬥，縣吏言五坊使下毆擊百姓。

translations.literal: Earlier, Magistrate Cui Fa of Hu County heard a clamorous fight outside the gate; a county clerk said men under the Five Wards commissioners were beating commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Fa, magistrate of Hu County, heard a commotion outside the gate; a clerk reported that men from the Five Wards commissioners' office were beating commoners.

sentences.zh: 發怒，命吏捕之。

translations.literal: Fa grew angry and ordered clerks to arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: Fa was enraged and ordered his clerks to arrest them.

sentences.zh: 曳挾既至，時已曛黑，不問色目。

translations.literal: They were dragged and brought in; by then it was already dusk-dark, and he did not ask their appearance.
translations.idiomatic: They were dragged in; by then it was dark, and he did not ask who they were.

sentences.zh: 良久與語，乃知是一內官。

translations.literal: After a long while in conversation he then learned it was an inner palace official.
translations.idiomatic: Only after speaking with them at length did he learn that one was an inner-palace eunuch.

sentences.zh: 天子聞之怒，收發系御史臺。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven heard of it he was angry and had Fa taken and bound in the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he was furious and had Fa arrested and held in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 禦樓之日，放系囚，發亦在雞竿下。

translations.literal: On the day of the imperial tower audience, bound prisoners were released, and Fa was also beneath the cock pole.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the imperial tower amnesty, prisoners were released, and Fa stood beneath the cock pole with the rest.

sentences.zh: 時有品官五十余人，持仗毆發，縱橫亂擊，發破面折齒。

translations.literal: At the time more than fifty ranked officials, holding staves, beat Fa, striking wildly in all directions; Fa's face was broken and his teeth knocked out.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty ranked officials then set upon him with staves, striking wildly; Fa's face was broken and his teeth knocked out.

sentences.zh: 臺吏以席蔽之，方免。

translations.literal: Censorate clerks shielded him with mats before he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate clerks shielded him with mats before he escaped further harm.

sentences.zh: 是日系囚皆釋，發獨不免。

translations.literal: That day all bound prisoners were released, but Fa alone was not spared.
translations.idiomatic: That day every prisoner was released except Fa.

sentences.zh: 渤疏論之曰：「縣令不合曳中人，中人不合毆禦囚，其罪一也。

translations.literal: Bo submitted a memorial discussing it, saying: "The magistrate should not have dragged an inner official; the inner official should not have beaten a prisoner under imperial guard—each is one offense.
translations.idiomatic: Bo memorialized: "The magistrate should not have dragged a palace eunuch, and the eunuch should not have beaten a prisoner under guard—the offenses are comparable.

sentences.zh: 然縣令所犯在恩前，中人所犯在恩後。

translations.literal: Yet the magistrate's offense occurred before the grace, while the inner official's offense occurred after the grace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the magistrate's offense came before the amnesty, while the eunuch's came after it.

sentences.zh: 中人橫暴，一至於此，是朝廷馴致使然。

translations.literal: Inner officials' violence and arrogance reached to this degree—it is because the court has tamed and led them to it.
translations.idiomatic: That palace eunuchs could be so violent shows how the court has indulged them.

sentences.zh: 若不早正刑書，臣恐四夷之人及籓鎮奏事傳道此語，則慢易之心萌矣。」

translations.literal: If we do not early rectify the penal code, your servant fears that men of the four barbarians and regional commands reporting affairs will spread this saying abroad, and a heart of contempt and ease will arise."
translations.idiomatic: Unless the law is enforced soon, I fear foreign envoys and regional commissioners will hear of this and contempt for the throne will take root."

sentences.zh: 渤又宣言於朝云：「郊禮前一日，兩神策軍於青城內奪京兆府進食牙盤，不時處置，致有毆擊崔發之事。」

translations.literal: Bo also proclaimed at court, saying: "On the day before the suburban sacrifice, the two Divine Strategy Armies within the Green Citadel seized the tooth-trays of food presented by the Metropolitan Prefecture, and because this was not handled in timely fashion, it led to the beating of Cui Fa."
translations.idiomatic: Bo also declared at court: "On the eve of the suburban sacrifice, troops of the two Divine Strategy Armies seized food trays presented by the Metropolitan Prefecture inside the Green Citadel; because nothing was done in time, the beating of Cui Fa followed."

sentences.zh: 上聞之，按問左右，皆言無奪食事。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he investigated those around him, and all said there was no seizure of food.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he questioned those around him, and all denied any seizure of food.

sentences.zh: 以渤黨發，出為桂州刺史、兼御史中丞，充桂管都防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: Because Bo sided with Fa, he was sent out as prefect of Guizhou and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, serving as Guiguan overall defense and observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Bo partial to Fa, the court sent him out as prefect of Guizhou and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, with overall defense and observation authority over Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 渤雖被斥，正論不已，而諫官繼論其屈。

translations.literal: Though Bo was dismissed, his upright discourse did not cease, and remonstrance officials continued to discuss his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Though Bo had been dismissed, he did not cease his forthright criticism, and remonstrance officials kept arguing that he had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 後宰相李逢吉、竇易直、李程因延英上語及崔發，逢吉等奏曰：「崔發淩轢中人，誠大不敬。

translations.literal: Later chief ministers Li Fengji, Dou Yizhi, and Li Cheng, because of words at the Yanchi audience concerning Cui Fa, memorialized, saying: "Cui Fa insulted and trampled an inner official—truly a great lack of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at an Yanchi audience, chief ministers Li Fengji, Dou Yizhi, and Li Cheng spoke of Cui Fa and memorialized: "Cui Fa insulted a palace eunuch—a grave lack of respect.

sentences.zh: 然發母是故相韋貫之姊，年僅八十。

translations.literal: Yet Fa's mother is the elder sister of the former chief minister Wei Guanzhi and is barely eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fa's mother is the elder sister of former chief minister Wei Guanzhi and is nearly eighty.

sentences.zh: 自發下獄，積憂成疾。

translations.literal: Since Fa entered prison, accumulated grief has become illness.
translations.idiomatic: Since Fa was imprisoned she has been stricken with grief and illness.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下孝治天下，稍垂恩宥。」

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty governs the realm through filial piety and might slightly extend gracious pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty governs the realm through filial piety; we beg a small measure of grace."

sentences.zh: 帝湣然良久，曰：「比諫官論奏，但言發屈，未嘗言不敬之罪，亦不言有老母。

translations.literal: The emperor looked pitying for a long while and said: "Recently when remonstrance officials discussed and memorialized, they only spoke of Fa's grievance and never said there was an offense of disrespect, nor did they speak of his having an aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved for a long moment and said: "When remonstrance officials spoke of this lately, they mentioned only that Fa had been wronged—they never spoke of the offense of disrespect, nor that he had an aged mother.

sentences.zh: 如卿等言，寧無湣惻！」

translations.literal: As you speak, how could there be no pity and compassion!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing you speak thus, how could I not feel compassion!"

sentences.zh: 即遣中使送發至其家，兼撫問發母。

translations.literal: He immediately sent a palace envoy to escort Fa to his home and also to comfort and inquire after Fa's mother.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once sent a palace envoy to take Fa home and to comfort his mother.

sentences.zh: 韋夫人號哭，對中使杖發四十，拜章謝恩。

translations.literal: Lady Wei wailed aloud; facing the palace envoy she had Fa beaten forty strokes and submitted a memorial thanking the grace.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei wept aloud; before the envoy she had Fa beaten forty strokes and submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣中使慰安之。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent a palace envoy to comfort and reassure her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent an envoy to comfort her.

sentences.zh: 渤在桂管二年，風恙求代，罷歸洛陽。

translations.literal: Bo spent two years in Guiguan, then because of wind ailment requested a replacement and was dismissed to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in Guiguan, Bo fell ill with wind ailment, sought a successor, and retired to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，以太子賓客征至京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he was summoned to the capital as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he was recalled to the capital as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 月余卒，時年五十九，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month he died, aged fifty-nine; he was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he died at fifty-nine and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 渤孤貞，力行操尚，不茍合，而阘茸之流，非其沽激。

translations.literal: Bo was solitary and upright, vigorously practicing moral integrity, not compromising—and the base and incompetent sort were not his audience for stirring reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was solitary and upright, devoted to principle, and would not compromise; the base and incompetent were not the audience he sought to impress.

sentences.zh: 至於以言擯退，終不息言，以救時病，服名節者重之。

translations.literal: As for being driven out by his words, he never ceased speaking, to remedy the ills of the age; those who valued reputation and integrity held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Even when his words got him dismissed, he never stopped speaking to remedy the ills of the age; men who valued integrity esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 子祝，會昌中登進士第，辟諸侯府。

translations.literal: His son Zhu, in the Huichang era passed the jinshi examination and was recruited into a regional lord's staff.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu passed the jinshi examination in the Huichang era and entered service in a regional commander's staff.

sentences.zh: 張仲方，韶州始興人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongfang—Zhang Zhongfang was a native of Shixing in Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongfang was a native of Shixing in Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 祖九臯，廣州刺史、殿中監、嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jiugao was prefect of Guangzhou, Director of the Palace Domestic Service, and Lingnan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiugao had served as prefect of Guangzhou, director of the palace domestic service, and Lingnan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 父抗，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: His father Kang was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kang was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 仲方伯祖始興文獻公九齡，開元朝名相。

translations.literal: Zhongfang's great-uncle was Jiuling, Duke Wenxian of Shixing, a famous chief minister of the Kaiyuan reign.
translations.idiomatic: His great-uncle was Zhang Jiuling, Duke Wenxian of Shixing, the renowned Kaiyuan chief minister.

sentences.zh: 仲方，貞元中進士擢第，宏辭登科，釋褐集賢校理，丁母憂免。

translations.literal: Zhongfang, in the Zhenyuan era passed the jinshi selection, passed the macro-literary examination, left the sackcloth as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang passed the jinshi in the Zhenyuan era and the macro-literary examination, took his first post as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補秘書省正字，調授咸陽尉。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Standardizer in the Secretariat and transferred to serve as magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became a standardizer in the Secretariat and was assigned as magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 出為邠州從事，入朝歷侍御史、倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: He went out as staff member in Binzhou, entered court and successively served as attendant censor and vice director in the Bureau of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staff in Binzhou, then returned to court as attendant censor and vice director in the Bureau of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 會呂溫、羊士諤誣告宰相李吉甫陰事，二人俱貶。

translations.literal: It happened that Lü Wen and Yang Shiru falsely reported secret affairs of Chief Minister Li Jiji; both were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Wen and Yang Shiru falsely accused Chief Minister Li Jiji of secret misconduct, both were demoted.

sentences.zh: 仲方坐呂溫貢舉門生，出為金州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhongfang, implicated as Lü Wen's examination protégé, was sent out as prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang, linked to Lü Wen as his examination protégé, was sent out as prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 吉甫卒，入為度支郎中。

translations.literal: When Jiji died, Zhongfang entered the capital as director in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiji's death he was recalled as director in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時太常定吉甫謚為「恭懿」，博士尉遲汾請為「敬憲」，仲方駁議曰：古者，易名請謚，禮之典也。

translations.literal: At that time the Court of Imperial Sacrifices fixed Jiji's posthumous title as "Gongyi"; Erudite Yuchi Fen requested "Jingxian"; Zhongfang rebutted in argument, saying: In antiquity, changing the name and requesting a posthumous title was a canonical rite.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Court of Imperial Sacrifices fixed Jiji's posthumous title as "Gongyi"; Erudite Yuchi Fen requested "Jingxian"; Zhongfang rebutted, saying: In antiquity, changing the name and requesting a posthumous title was a canonical rite.

sentences.zh: 處大位者，取其巨節，蔑諸細行，垂範當代，昭示後人，然後書之，垂於不朽。

translations.literal: One who occupies a great position should take his major integrity, disregard minor conduct, set an example for the age, make clear to later generations, and only then record it, to endure in imperishability.
translations.idiomatic: One who occupies a great position should take his major integrity, disregard minor conduct, set an example for the age, make clear to later generations, and only then record it for imperishable fame.

sentences.zh: 善善惡惡，不可以誣，故稱一字，則至明矣；

translations.literal: Praising the good and condemning the evil cannot be falsified; therefore in naming a single character, the meaning is then most clear;
translations.idiomatic: Praising the good and condemning the evil cannot be falsified; therefore a single character makes the meaning perfectly clear;

sentences.zh: 定褒貶是非之宜，泯同異紛綸之論。

translations.literal: it fixes what is fitting in praise and blame, right and wrong, and extinguishes tangled disputes of agreement and difference.
translations.idiomatic: it fixes what is fitting in praise and blame and extinguishes tangled disputes of agreement and difference.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒吉甫，稟氣生材，乘時佐治，博涉多藝，含章炳文。

translations.literal: The posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor Jiji received vital force and produced talent, seized the time to assist in governance, broadly traversed many arts, and contained brilliance and luminous composition.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor Jiji was naturally gifted, rose with the times to aid governance, was broadly learned in many arts, and brilliant in composition.

sentences.zh: 燮贊陰陽，經緯邦國。

translations.literal: He harmonized yin and yang and organized the state.
translations.idiomatic: He harmonized yin and yang and organized the state.

sentences.zh: 惜乎通敏資性，便媚取容。

translations.literal: Alas, he was quick and clever by nature, skilled at flattery to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, he was quick and clever by nature and skilled at flattery to win favor.

sentences.zh: 故載踐樞衡，疊致臺袞，大權在己，沈謀罕成，好惡徇情，輕諾寡信。

translations.literal: Therefore he repeatedly reached the pivot of power, accumulated high ministerial rank, kept great authority in his own hands, rarely completed deep schemes, indulged likes and dislikes according to personal feeling, made light promises and kept little faith.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he repeatedly reached the highest offices, accumulated multiple ministerial ranks, kept great authority in his own hands, rarely completed deep schemes, indulged personal likes and dislikes, made light promises and kept little faith.

sentences.zh: 諂淚在臉，遇便則流；

translations.literal: Flattering tears were on his face; when opportunity appeared they flowed;
translations.idiomatic: Flattering tears were on his face; when opportunity appeared they flowed;

sentences.zh: 巧言如簧，應機必發。

translations.literal: Clever words were like a reed organ; when the moment came they were sure to spring forth.
translations.idiomatic: Clever words were like a reed organ; when the moment came they were sure to spring forth.

sentences.zh: 夫人臣之翼戴元後者，端恪致治，孜孜夙夜，絹熙庶績，平章百揆。

translations.literal: Now a minister who supports and upholds the sovereign should govern with rectitude and diligence, work earnestly day and night, bring brilliance to the myriad achievements, and harmonize the hundred duties.
translations.idiomatic: A minister who supports and upholds the sovereign should govern with rectitude and diligence, work earnestly day and night, bring brilliance to the myriad achievements, and harmonize the hundred duties.

sentences.zh: 兵者兇器，不可從我始；

translations.literal: Arms are instruments of calamity—they must not begin with me;
translations.idiomatic: Arms are instruments of calamity—they must not begin with me;

sentences.zh: 及乎伐罪，則料敵以成功。

translations.literal: Only when punishing crime should one measure the enemy to achieve success.
translations.idiomatic: Only when punishing crime should one measure the enemy to achieve success.

sentences.zh: 至使內有害輔臣之盜，外有懷毒蠆之孽。

translations.literal: This led to having within harmful thieves among assisting ministers and without poisonous scorpion-like evils harboring malice.
translations.idiomatic: This led to harmful thieves among assisting ministers within and poisonous scorpion-like evils harboring malice without.

sentences.zh: 師徒暴野，戎馬生郊。

translations.literal: Armies and troops lay exposed in the fields; warhorses bred in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Armies lay exposed in the fields and warhorses bred at the capital's edge.

sentences.zh: 皇上旰食宵衣，公卿大夫且慚且恥。

translations.literal: The emperor skipped meals and slept little in his robes; dukes, ministers, and grandees were both ashamed and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor skipped meals and slept little in his robes; dukes, ministers, and grandees were both ashamed and humiliated.

sentences.zh: 農人不得在畝，緝婦不得在桑。

translations.literal: Farmers could not be in the furrows; silk workers could not be at the mulberry trees.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers could not work their fields; silk workers could not tend their mulberry trees.

sentences.zh: 耗斂賦之常貲，散帑廩之中積；

translations.literal: Regular revenues of taxation were exhausted; accumulations in the treasury granaries were dispersed;
translations.idiomatic: Regular tax revenues were exhausted and storehouse grain was dispersed;

sentences.zh: 征邊僥之備，竭運挽之勞。

translations.literal: frontier contingents were levied for defense; transport and hauling labor was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: frontier contingents were levied and transport labor was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 僵屍血流，胔骼成嶽，酷毒之痛，號訴無辜，剿絕群生，逮今四載。

translations.literal: Corpses stiffened and blood flowed; flesh and bones formed hills; cruel and poisonous pain, cries of the innocent, cutting off all living beings—down to today, four years.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses stiffened and blood flowed; flesh and bones piled like hills; cruel pain and the cries of the innocent cut off all living beings—for four years now.

sentences.zh: 禍胎之兆，實始其謀；

translations.literal: The omen of the embryo of disaster truly began in his scheming;
translations.idiomatic: The seeds of disaster truly began in his scheming;

sentences.zh: 遺君父之憂，而豈謂之先覺者乎？

translations.literal: He left worry to ruler and father—how can he be called one who foresaw beforehand?
translations.idiomatic: He left worry to ruler and father—how can he be called one who foresaw beforehand?

sentences.zh: 夫論大功者，不可以妄取，不可以枉致。

translations.literal: In discussing great merit, one must not seize it rashly or seize it wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: In discussing great merit, one must not seize it rashly or seize it wrongly.

sentences.zh: 為資畫者體理，不顯不競，而豈妨令美？

translations.literal: For one who draws up plans, modest restraint in form and principle, not displaying and not contending—how would that obstruct true excellence?
translations.idiomatic: For one who draws up plans, modest restraint does not display or contend—how would that obstruct true excellence?

sentences.zh: 當削平西蜀，乃言語侍從之臣；

translations.literal: When the western Shu was conquered and pacified, he was merely a literary attendant;
translations.idiomatic: When western Shu was conquered and pacified, he was merely a literary attendant;

sentences.zh: 擒翦東吳，則訏謨廊廟之輔。

translations.literal: when eastern Wu was captured and cut down, he was then a counselor in the hall and temple.
translations.idiomatic: when eastern Wu was captured and cut down, he was then a chief counselor of the hall.

sentences.zh: 較其功則有異，言其力則不倫。

translations.literal: Comparing their achievements, they differ; speaking of their strength, they do not match.
translations.idiomatic: Their achievements differ and their exerted strength does not match.

sentences.zh: 何舍其所重而錄其所輕，收其所小而略其所大？

translations.literal: Why abandon what is weighty and record what is light, gather what is small and overlook what is great?
translations.idiomatic: Why abandon what is weighty and record what is light, gather what is small and overlook what is great?

sentences.zh: 且奢靡是嗜，而曰愛人以儉；

translations.literal: Moreover, he was addicted to luxury, yet said he loved people through thrift;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he was addicted to luxury yet claimed to love people through thrift;

sentences.zh: 受授無守，而曰慎才以補。

translations.literal: he accepted appointments without holding to them, yet said he carefully selected talent for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: he accepted appointments without holding to them yet claimed to carefully select talent for appointment.

sentences.zh: 斥諫諍之士於外，豈不近之蔽聰乎？

translations.literal: He drove remonstrance ministers outside—was this not the ruler's deafness through intimacy?
translations.idiomatic: He drove remonstrance ministers outside—was this not deafening the ruler through intimacy?

sentences.zh: 舉忠烈之廟於內，豈不近之昵愛也？

translations.literal: He promoted shrines of loyal martyrs within—was this not the ruler's favoritism through intimacy?
translations.idiomatic: He promoted shrines of loyal martyrs within—was this not favoring the ruler through intimacy?

sentences.zh: 焉有蔽聰昵愛，家範無制，而能垂法作程，憲章百度乎？

translations.literal: How can one who deafens and favors through intimacy, with no household discipline, yet set law as model and regulate the hundred measures?
translations.idiomatic: How can one who deafens and favors through intimacy, with no household discipline, yet set law as model and regulate the hundred measures?

sentences.zh: 謹按謚法，敬以直內，內而不肅，何以刑於外？

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the posthumous law: "Jing" means rectifying the inner; if the inner is not reverent, how can one be a model without?
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examining the posthumous law: "Jing" means rectifying the inner; if the inner is not reverent, how can one be a model without?

sentences.zh: 憲者，法也。

translations.literal: "Xian" means law.
translations.idiomatic: "Xian" means law.

sentences.zh: 《戴記》曰：「憲章文武。」

translations.literal: The Record of Dai says, "Take law and model from Wen and Wu."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Dai says, "Take law and model from Wen and Wu."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「發慮憲。」

translations.literal: It also says, "Give thought to law."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Give thought to law."

sentences.zh: 義以為敬恪終始，載考歷位，未嘗效一法官，議一小獄。

translations.literal: In meaning, one should be reverent and diligent from start to finish; reviewing his career in office, he never once judged a single legal case or discussed a single lawsuit.
translations.idiomatic: In meaning, one should be reverent and diligent from start to finish; reviewing his career in office, he never once judged a single legal case or discussed a single lawsuit.

sentences.zh: 及居重位，以安和平易寬柔自處。

translations.literal: When he occupied a weighty position, he took ease, peace, tolerance, and gentleness as his manner.
translations.idiomatic: When he occupied a weighty position, he took ease, peace, tolerance, and gentleness as his manner.

sentences.zh: 考其名，與其行不類；

translations.literal: Examining his name against his conduct, they do not match;
translations.idiomatic: Examining his name against his conduct, they do not match;

sentences.zh: 研其事，與其道不侔。

translations.literal: examining his deeds against the Way, they do not accord.
translations.idiomatic: examining his deeds against the Way, they do not accord.

sentences.zh: 一定之辭，惟精惟審，異日詳制，貽諸史官。

translations.literal: With a settled word, with utmost refinement and scrutiny, on another day the full designation will be made and bequeathed to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: With a settled word, with utmost refinement and scrutiny, on another day the full designation will be made and bequeathed to the historiographers.

sentences.zh: 請俟蔡寇將平，天下無事，然後都堂聚議，謚亦未遲。

translations.literal: Please wait until the Cai bandit is nearly pacified and all under Heaven is without affair; then the chief hall can assemble to discuss—the posthumous name is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: Please wait until the Cai bandit is nearly pacified and all under Heaven is at peace; then the chief hall can assemble to discuss—the posthumous name is not yet late.

sentences.zh: 憲宗方用兵，惡仲方深言其事，怒甚，貶為遂州司馬，量移復州司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was then deploying troops and hated that Zhongfang spoke deeply on this matter; greatly angered, he demoted him to military adjutant of Suizhou, then transferred him by quota to military adjutant of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was at war and resented Zhongfang's blunt argument on the matter; in great anger he demoted him to military adjutant of Suizhou, then transferred him to the same post in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷河東少尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 滎陽大海佛寺，有高祖為隋鄭州刺史日，為太宗疾祈福，於此寺造石像一軀，凡刊勒十六字以誌之。

translations.literal: At the Dahai Buddhist Temple in Xingyang there was a stone image of one body that Gaozu, when he was Sui prefect of Zhengzhou, had made in this temple to pray for blessings when Taizong was ill; in all sixteen characters were carved and inscribed to record it.
translations.idiomatic: At the Dahai Buddhist Temple in Xingyang stood a stone image that Gaozu, when he was Sui prefect of Zhengzhou, had commissioned there to pray for Taizong's recovery; sixteen characters were carved on it as a record.

sentences.zh: 歲久剚缺，滎陽令李光慶重加修飾，仲方再刊石記之以聞。

translations.literal: After years the carving was damaged and missing; Magistrate Li Guangqing of Xingyang restored and ornamented it anew; Zhongfang again carved a stone record and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: After years the inscription had worn away; Magistrate Li Guangqing of Xingyang restored it, and Zhongfang had the stone record recarved and reported the matter to court.

sentences.zh: 及敬宗即位，李程作相，與仲方同年登進士第，召仲方為右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Li Cheng became chief minister; he and Zhongfang had passed the jinshi in the same year, and Zhongfang was summoned as Right Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne, Li Cheng became chief minister; he and Zhongfang had passed the jinshi in the same year, and Zhongfang was recalled as Right Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 敬宗童年戲慢，詔淮南王播造上巳競渡船三十只。

translations.literal: Jingzong in his youth was playful and disrespectful; he ordered Prince of Huainan Wang Bo to build thirty dragon-boat racing vessels for the Shangsi festival.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong in his youth was frivolous and ordered Prince of Huainan Wang Bo to build thirty dragon boats for the Shangsi festival.

sentences.zh: 播將船材於京師造作，計用半年轉運之費方得成。

translations.literal: Bo was to fashion the boat timber in the capital; it was calculated that half a year's transport costs would be needed before completion.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was to build the boats in the capital from timber shipped there—at a cost of half a year's transport expenses before they could be finished.

sentences.zh: 仲方詣延英面論，言甚懇激。

translations.literal: Zhongfang went to the Yanchi audience and argued face to face, his words very earnest and impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang argued the matter face to face at an Yanchi audience, speaking with great earnestness.

sentences.zh: 帝只令造十只以進。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered only ten built and presented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered only ten built instead.

sentences.zh: 帝又欲幸華清宮，仲方諫曰：「萬乘所幸，出須備儀。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to visit Huaqing Palace; Zhongfang remonstrated, saying: "Where the ruler of ten thousand chariots goes, departure requires full ceremonial escort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished to visit Huaqing Palace; Zhongfang remonstrated: "When the Son of Heaven travels abroad, he must go with full ceremonial escort.

sentences.zh: 無宜輕行，以失威重。」

translations.literal: It is not fitting to travel lightly and thereby lose majesty and weight."
translations.idiomatic: He should not travel lightly and forfeit his majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝雖不從，慰勞之。

translations.literal: Though the emperor did not follow his advice, he comforted and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him but comforted and praised him.

sentences.zh: 太和初，出為福州刺史、兼御史中丞、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was sent out as prefect of Fuzhou, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Fujian Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe he was sent out as prefect of Fuzhou, concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and Fujian observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，入為太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered the capital as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，轉右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year he was transferred to Right Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year he became Right Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 七年，李德裕輔政，出為太子賓客分司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Li Deyu assisted in government; Zhongfang was sent out as Mentor of the Heir Apparent with detached assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Li Deyu came to power, Zhongfang was given a detached post as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 八年，德裕罷相，李守閔復召仲方為常侍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Deyu left the chief ministership; Li Shoumin again summoned Zhongfang as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after Deyu left office, Li Shoumin recalled Zhongfang as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 九年十一月，李訓之亂，四宰相、中丞、京兆尹皆死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year, in the turmoil of Li Xun, four chief ministers, the vice censor-in-chief, and the metropolitan governor all died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the ninth year, during Li Xun's coup, four chief ministers, the vice censor-in-chief, and the metropolitan governor were all killed.

sentences.zh: 翌日，兩省官入朝。

translations.literal: The next day officials of the two departments entered court.
translations.idiomatic: The next day officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery attended court.

sentences.zh: 宣政衙門未開，百官錯立於朝堂，無人吏引接。

translations.literal: The Xuanzheng yamen gate had not opened; the hundred officials stood confused in the court hall with no clerks to guide them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzheng gate had not opened; officials stood in confusion in the court hall with no attendants to guide them.

sentences.zh: 逡巡，閣門使馬元贄斜開宣政衙門傳宣曰：「有敕召左散騎常侍張仲方。」

translations.literal: After a while Gate Commissioner Ma Yuanzan partly opened the Xuanzheng yamen gate and announced: "There is an edict summoning Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Zhongfang."
translations.idiomatic: After a while Gate Commissioner Ma Yuanzan partly opened the Xuanzheng gate and announced: "By edict, summon Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Zhongfang."

sentences.zh: 仲方出班。

translations.literal: Zhongfang stepped out of the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang stepped forward from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 元贄宣曰：「仲方可京兆尹。」

translations.literal: Yuanzan announced: "Zhongfang may be Metropolitan Governor."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzan announced: "Zhongfang is appointed Metropolitan Governor."

sentences.zh: 然後衙門大開，喚仗。

translations.literal: Only then was the yamen gate fully opened and the guard summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was the gate fully opened and the guard summoned.

sentences.zh: 月余，鄭覃作相，用薛元賞為京兆尹，出仲方為華州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a month Zheng Tan became chief minister, employed Xue Yuanshang as metropolitan governor, and sent Zhongfang out as prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later Zheng Tan became chief minister, appointed Xue Yuanshang metropolitan governor, and sent Zhongfang out as prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 開成元年五月，入為秘書監。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Kaicheng he entered as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Kaicheng he was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 外議以鄭覃黨李德裕，排擯仲方。

translations.literal: Outside opinion held that Zheng Tan sided with Li Deyu and pushed Zhongfang aside.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that Zheng Tan, aligned with Li Deyu, had pushed Zhongfang aside.

sentences.zh: 覃恐涉朋黨，因紫宸奏事，覃啟曰：「丞郎闕人，臣欲用張仲方。」

translations.literal: Tan feared being implicated in faction; during an audience at Zichen he opened, saying: "There is a vacancy among the vice directors; your servant wishes to employ Zhang Zhongfang."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the appearance of faction, Tan spoke at a Zichen audience: "There is a vacancy among the vice directors; I wish to appoint Zhang Zhongfang."

sentences.zh: 文宗曰：「中臺侍郎，朝廷華選。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong said: "Vice directors of the Central Terrace are splendid selections of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong said: "Vice directors of the Central Terrace are the court's finest appointments.

sentences.zh: 仲方作牧守無政，安可以丞郎處之？」

translations.literal: Zhongfang as prefect and defender had no achievement in government—how can he be placed in a vice director's post?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang achieved nothing as a regional governor—how can he hold a vice director's post?"

sentences.zh: 累加銀青光祿大夫、上柱國、曲江縣開國伯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Upper Pillar of the State, Baron of Qujiang County with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Upper Pillar of the State, and Baron of Qujiang with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二年四月卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of the second year.

sentences.zh: 仲方貞確自立，綽有祖風。

translations.literal: Zhongfang was upright and established himself independently, abundantly possessing his ancestor's style.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang was upright and self-reliant and bore his ancestor's manner in full measure.

sentences.zh: 自駁謚之後，為德裕之黨擯斥，坎坷而歿，人士輩之。

translations.literal: From the time of his posthumous-title rebuttal onward, he was pushed aside by Deyu's faction, ended his life in hardship, and gentlemen of the age sympathized with him.
translations.idiomatic: After his rebuttal over Jiji's posthumous title he was sidelined by Deyu's faction, lived out his days in frustration, and men of the age pitied him.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 兄仲端，位終都昌令。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhongduan ended his career as magistrate of Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhongduan ended his career as magistrate of Duchang.

sentences.zh: 弟仲孚，登進士第，為監察御史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhongfu passed the jinshi and served as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhongfu passed the jinshi and served as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 裴潾，河東人也。

translations.literal: Pei Lin—Pei Lin was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Lin was a native of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，善隸書。

translations.literal: In youth he was devoted to study and skilled in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was devoted to learning and skilled in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 以門廕入仕。

translations.literal: He entered office through hereditary privilege by his family's standing.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 元和初，累遷右拾遺，轉左補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was repeatedly promoted to Right Reminder and transferred to Left Supplements-the-Omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he rose to Right Reminder and then Left Supplements-the-Omissions.

sentences.zh: 元和中，兩河用兵。

translations.literal: During Yuanhe troops were deployed in the two He regions.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhe the court campaigned in the two He regions.

sentences.zh: 初，憲宗寵任內官，有至專兵柄者，又以內官充館驛使。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Xianzong favored and employed inner officials, some even monopolizing military authority, and also used inner officials as relay-station commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Xianzong favored palace eunuchs, some of whom even held military power, and also appointed them relay-station commissioners.

sentences.zh: 有曹進玉者，恃恩暴戾，遇四方使多倨，有至捽辱者，宰相李吉甫奏罷之。

translations.literal: There was one Cao Jinyu who relied on favor and was violent and cruel; meeting envoys from the four directions he was often arrogant, and some he even seized and insulted; Chief Minister Li Jiji memorialized to abolish the post.
translations.idiomatic: One Cao Jinyu, relying on imperial favor, was violent and arrogant toward envoys from the regions, sometimes seizing and humiliating them; Chief Minister Li Jiji memorialized to abolish the eunuch relay commissioners.

sentences.zh: 十二年，淮西用兵，復以內官為使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, with troops deployed in Huaixi, inner officials were again made commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, during the Huaixi campaign, inner officials were again appointed relay commissioners.

sentences.zh: 潾上疏曰：「館驛之務，每驛皆有專知官。

translations.literal: Lin submitted a memorial, saying: "The affairs of relay stations—each station has a dedicated supervising official.
translations.idiomatic: Lin memorialized: "Each relay station already has a dedicated supervisor for its affairs.

sentences.zh: 畿內有京兆尹，外道有觀察使、刺史叠相監臨；

translations.literal: Within the capital region there is the Metropolitan Governor; on outer routes there are observation commissioners and prefects who oversee one another in layers.
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital region the Metropolitan Governor oversees them; on outer routes observation commissioners and prefects supervise in turn.

sentences.zh: 臺中又有御史充館驛使，專察過闕。

translations.literal: In the Censorate there are also censors who serve as relay-station commissioners, specially inspecting faults and omissions.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate also assigns censors as relay commissioners to inspect faults.

sentences.zh: 伏知近有敗事，上聞聖聰。

translations.literal: I humbly know there have recently been failures reported to the sage awareness.
translations.idiomatic: Recent failures have, I know, reached Your Majesty's ear.

sentences.zh: 但明示科條，督責官吏，據其所犯，重加貶黜，敢不惕懼，日夜厲精。
