translations.literal: Only make the statutes clear, supervise and charge the officials, according to their offenses heavily demote and dismiss—who would not be vigilant and fearful and day and night sharpen their effort?
translations.idiomatic: Make the regulations clear, hold the officials accountable, and demote or dismiss according to offense—then who would not be vigilant and strive day and night?

sentences.zh: 若令宮闈之臣，出參館驛之務，則內臣外事，職分各殊，切在塞侵官之源，絕出位之漸。

translations.literal: If inner-palace persons are ordered to go out and participate in relay-station affairs, then inner persons in outer affairs—their duties are each distinct; it is urgent to block the source of encroaching on offices and cut off the gradual overstepping of position.
translations.idiomatic: If inner-palace eunuchs are sent out to manage relay stations, inner officials will handle outer affairs though their duties differ—urgently block this encroachment and cut off overreach at its start.

sentences.zh: 事有不便，必誡以初；

translations.literal: When affairs are inconvenient, one must warn at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: When a practice proves harmful, correct it at the outset.

sentences.zh: 令或有妨，不必在大。

translations.literal: Orders that may cause harm need not be great in scale.
translations.idiomatic: A harmful order need not be grand to do damage.

sentences.zh: 當掃靜妖氛之日，開太平至理之風。

translations.literal: At the time when evil vapors should be swept clean, open the wind of great peace and ultimate principle.
translations.idiomatic: This is the time to sweep away disorder and open the way to true peace.

sentences.zh: 澄本正名，實在今日。」

translations.literal: Clarifying the root and rectifying names truly lies in today."
translations.idiomatic: To clarify roles and restore proper names is the task of this moment."

sentences.zh: 言雖不用，帝意嘉之，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: Though his words were not adopted, the emperor's mind approved him and he was transferred to Diarist of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Though his advice was not followed, the emperor approved of it and promoted him to diarist of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 憲宗季年銳於服餌，詔天下搜訪奇士。

translations.literal: In his late years Emperor Xianzong was keen on taking medicines and elixirs and ordered the realm to search out extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years Emperor Xianzong was keen on elixirs and ordered the realm to search out wonder-workers.

sentences.zh: 宰相皇甫镈與金吾將軍李道古挾邪固寵，薦山人柳泌及僧大通、鳳翔人田佐元，皆待詔翰林。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Huangfu Bo and Golden Crow General Li Daogu, relying on wickedness to secure favor, recommended the mountain man Liu Bi, the monk Datong, and Tian Zuoyuan of Fengxiang—all awaiting edicts at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Huangfu Bo and Golden Crow general Li Daogu, relying on flattery to hold favor, recommended the wonder-worker Liu Bi, the monk Datong, and Tian Zuoyuan of Fengxiang—all given Hanlin posts awaiting edict.

sentences.zh: 憲宗服泌藥，日增躁渴，流聞於外。

translations.literal: Xianzong took Bi's medicine; day by day restlessness and thirst increased, and word spread outside.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong took Bi's elixir; his restlessness and thirst grew daily, and word spread beyond the palace.

sentences.zh: 潾上疏諫曰：臣聞除天下之害者，受天下之利；

translations.literal: Lin submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: This subject has heard that one who removes harm under Heaven receives benefit under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Lin submitted a memorial remonstrating: I have heard that one who removes harm under Heaven receives benefit under Heaven;

sentences.zh: 共天下之樂者，饗天下之福。

translations.literal: one who shares joy under Heaven enjoys blessing under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: one who shares joy under Heaven enjoys blessing under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故上自黃帝、顓頊、堯、舜、禹、湯，下及周文王、武王，鹹以功濟生靈，德配天地，故天皆報之以上壽，垂祚於無疆。

translations.literal: Therefore from above the Yellow Emperor, Zhuanxu, Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang, down to King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, all by merit rescued living beings, their virtue matching Heaven and Earth—therefore Heaven all repaid them with long life and extended their reigns without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from the Yellow Emperor, Zhuanxu, Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang down to King Wen and King Wu of Zhou, all by merit rescued living beings and matched Heaven and Earth in virtue—therefore Heaven repaid them all with long life and extended their reigns without limit.

sentences.zh: 伏見陛下以大孝安宗廟，以至仁牧黎元。

translations.literal: This subject humbly observes that Your Majesty, with great filial piety, settles the ancestral temple, and with utmost benevolence tends the common people.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that Your Majesty, with great filial piety, settles the ancestral temple and with utmost benevolence tends the common people.

sentences.zh: 自踐祚已來，刬積代之妖兇，開削平之洪業。

translations.literal: Since assuming the throne, you have cut down accumulated generations of demonic evils and opened the great enterprise of conquest and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Since assuming the throne, you have cut down accumulated generations of demonic evils and opened the great enterprise of conquest and pacification.

sentences.zh: 而禮敬宰輔，待以終始；

translations.literal: Moreover, you honor and respect chief ministers and treat them from start to finish;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you honor chief ministers and treat them from start to finish;

sentences.zh: 內能大斷，外寬小故。

translations.literal: within you can make great decisions; without you are lenient in small matters.
translations.idiomatic: within you can make great decisions; without you are lenient in small matters.

sentences.zh: 夫此神功聖化，皆自古聖主明君所不及，陛下躬親行之，實光映千古矣。

translations.literal: Now this divine achievement and sage transformation are what sage rulers and enlightened lords of antiquity could not reach; Your Majesty personally carries them out—truly your brilliance shines across a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: This divine achievement and sage transformation surpass what sage rulers and enlightened lords of antiquity could reach; Your Majesty personally carries them out—truly your brilliance shines across a thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 是則天地神祇，必報陛下以山嶽之壽；

translations.literal: Then Heaven and Earth and the spirits will surely repay Your Majesty with the longevity of mountains and peaks;
translations.idiomatic: Then Heaven and Earth and the spirits will surely repay Your Majesty with the longevity of mountains and peaks;

sentences.zh: 宗廟聖靈，必福陛下以億萬之齡；

translations.literal: the ancestral temple's sage spirits will surely bless Your Majesty with tens of millions of years;
translations.idiomatic: the ancestral temple's sage spirits will surely bless Your Majesty with tens of millions of years;

sentences.zh: 四海蒼生，鹹祈陛下以覆載之永。

translations.literal: the common people of the four seas all pray for Your Majesty the enduring cover and support of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: the common people of the four seas all pray for Your Majesty the enduring cover and support of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 自然萬靈保祐，聖壽無疆。

translations.literal: Naturally the myriad spirits will protect and bless, and sage longevity will be without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally the myriad spirits will protect and bless, and sage longevity will be without limit.

sentences.zh: 伏見自去年已來，諸處頻薦藥術之士，有韋山甫、柳泌等，或更相稱引，迄今狂謬，薦送漸多。

translations.literal: This subject humbly observes that since last year, various places have frequently recommended masters of medicinal arts—Wei Shanfu, Liu Bi, and others—some mutually praising and recommending one another; down to today their wild absurdity has grown, and recommendations sent forward have gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that since last year various places have frequently recommended masters of medicinal arts—Wei Shanfu, Liu Bi, and others—some mutually praising and recommending one another; down to today their wild absurdity has grown and recommendations sent forward have gradually increased.

sentences.zh: 臣伏以真仙有道之士，皆匿其名姓，無求於代，潛遁山林，滅影雲壑，唯恐人見，唯懼人聞。

translations.literal: This subject humbly considers that true immortals and men of the Way all conceal their names and surnames, seek nothing from the age, withdraw hidden into mountains and forests, and extinguish their shadows in clouded ravines, fearing only that people see them and dreading only that people hear of them.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that true immortals and men of the Way all conceal their names, seek nothing from the age, withdraw hidden into mountains and forests, and extinguish their shadows in clouded ravines, fearing only that people see them and dreading only that people hear of them.

sentences.zh: 豈肯幹謁公卿，自鬻其術？

translations.literal: How would they be willing to importune grandees and ministers and sell their arts themselves?
translations.idiomatic: How would they be willing to importune grandees and ministers and sell their arts themselves?

sentences.zh: 今者所有誇炫藥術者，必非知道之士。

translations.literal: Those who now boast and display medicinal arts must not be men who know the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Those who now boast and display medicinal arts cannot be men who know the Way.

sentences.zh: 鹹為求利而來，自言飛煉為神，以誘權貴賄賂。

translations.literal: All come seeking profit, claiming themselves to refine by flight into divinity, to entice the powerful and noble with bribes.
translations.idiomatic: All come seeking profit, claiming to refine elixirs into divinity, to entice the powerful and noble with bribes.

sentences.zh: 大言怪論，驚聽惑時，及其假偽敗露，曾不恥於逃遁。

translations.literal: Grand words and strange doctrines startle the ear and confuse the age; when their falsity and fraud are exposed, they are not even ashamed to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Grand words and strange doctrines startle the ear and confuse the age; when their falsity is exposed, they are not even ashamed to flee.

sentences.zh: 如此情狀，豈可保信其術，親餌其藥哉？

translations.literal: With such circumstances, how can one trust their arts and personally ingest their medicines?
translations.idiomatic: With such circumstances, how can one trust their arts and personally ingest their medicines?

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「夫人，食味別聲，被色而生者也。」

translations.literal: The Rites says, "Man is one who lives by distinguishing flavors in food, distinguishing sounds, and being affected by color."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites says, "Man is one who lives by distinguishing flavors in food, distinguishing sounds, and being affected by color."

sentences.zh: 《春秋左氏傳》曰：「味以行氣，氣以實誌。」

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals says, "Flavor moves the vital force; vital force fills the will."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals says, "Flavor moves the vital force; vital force fills the will."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「水火醯醢鹽梅，以烹魚肉。

translations.literal: It also says, "Water and fire, vinegar and pickled meat, salt and plum, are used to cook fish and flesh.
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Water and fire, vinegar and pickled meat, salt and plum, are used to cook fish and flesh.

sentences.zh: 宰夫和之，齊之以味；

translations.literal: The cook harmonizes them and adjusts them with flavor;
translations.idiomatic: The cook harmonizes them and adjusts them with flavor;

sentences.zh: 君子食之，以平其心。」

translations.literal: the gentleman eats them to settle his heart."
translations.idiomatic: the gentleman eats them to settle his heart."

sentences.zh: 夫三牲五谷，稟自五行，發為五味，蓋天地生之所以奉人也，是以聖人節而食之，以致康強逢吉之福。

translations.literal: Now the three sacrificial animals and the five grains receive from the five phases and issue as the five flavors—this is how Heaven and Earth in producing things serve mankind; therefore the sage moderates in eating them to attain the blessing of health, strength, and encountering good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The three sacrificial animals and the five grains receive from the five phases and issue as the five flavors—this is how Heaven and Earth in producing things serve mankind; therefore the sage moderates in eating them to attain the blessing of health, strength, and good fortune.

sentences.zh: 若夫藥石者，前聖以之療疾，蓋非常食之物。

translations.literal: As for medicines and stones, former sages used them to treat illness—they are not foods for ordinary consumption.
translations.idiomatic: As for medicines and stones, former sages used them to treat illness—they are not foods for ordinary consumption.

sentences.zh: 況金石皆含酷烈熱毒之性，加以燒治，動經歲月，既兼烈火之氣，必恐難為防制。

translations.literal: Moreover, metal and stone all contain fierce, hot, and poisonous natures; added to this is firing and refining, often lasting months and years—they already combine the qi of fierce fire; one must fear they are hard to guard against and control.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, metal and stone all contain fierce, hot, and poisonous natures; with firing and refining often lasting months and years, they already combine the qi of fierce fire—one must fear they are hard to guard against and control.

sentences.zh: 若乃遠征前史，則秦、漢之君，皆信方士，如盧生、徐福、欒大、李少君，其後皆奸偽事發，其藥竟無所成。

translations.literal: If one goes far to cite earlier history, then the rulers of Qin and Han all trusted alchemical masters such as Lu Sheng, Xu Fu, Luan Da, and Li Shaojun; afterward fraud and falsity were all exposed, and their medicines in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: If one cites earlier history, the rulers of Qin and Han all trusted alchemical masters such as Lu Sheng, Xu Fu, Luan Da, and Li Shaojun; afterward fraud was exposed and their medicines achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 事著《史記》、《漢書》，皆可驗視。

translations.literal: The affairs are recorded in the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han—all can be verified and examined.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs are recorded in the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han—all can be verified and examined.

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「君之藥，臣先嘗之；

translations.literal: The Rites says, "The ruler's medicine—the minister tastes it first;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites says, "The ruler's medicine—the minister tastes it first;

sentences.zh: 親之藥，子先嘗之。」

translations.literal: the parent's medicine—the son tastes it first."
translations.idiomatic: the parent's medicine—the son tastes it first."

sentences.zh: 臣子一也，臣願所有金石，煉藥人及所薦之人，皆先服一年，以考其真偽，則自然明驗矣。

translations.literal: Minister and son are one; this subject wishes that all those who refine metal and stone medicines and all those recommended should first ingest them for one year, to test their truth and falsity—then naturally the proof will be clear.
translations.idiomatic: Minister and son are one; I wish that all those who refine metal and stone medicines and all those recommended should first ingest them for one year to test their truth and falsity—then the proof will be clear.

sentences.zh: 伏惟元和聖文神武法天應道皇帝陛下，合日月照臨之明，稟乾元利貞之德，崇正若指南，受諫如轉規，是必發精金之刃，斷可疑之網。

translations.literal: This subject humbly considers that the Yuanhe Sage Literary Divine Martial Emperor Who Aligns with Heaven and Responds to the Way, Your Majesty, combines the brightness of sun and moon shining down, receives the virtue of Qian's origination, benefit, firmness, and correctness, honors the upright as if pointing south, and accepts remonstrance as if turning a compass—surely you will draw the sharp blade of refined metal and cut the doubtful net.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, the Yuanhe Sage Literary Divine Martial Emperor Who Aligns with Heaven and Responds to the Way, combines the brightness of sun and moon shining down, receives the virtue of Qian's origination, benefit, firmness, and correctness, honors the upright as if pointing south, and accepts remonstrance as if turning a compass—surely you will draw the sharp blade of refined metal and cut the doubtful net.

sentences.zh: 所有藥術虛誕之徒，伏乞特賜罷遣，禁其幻惑。

translations.literal: All those of empty and absurd medicinal arts, this subject humbly begs that they be specially dismissed and sent away, and their delusive enchantments forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: All those of empty and absurd medicinal arts, I humbly beg that they be specially dismissed and sent away, and their delusive enchantments forbidden.

sentences.zh: 使浮雲盡徹，朗日增輝；

translations.literal: Let floating clouds be entirely cleared away and the bright sun increase in radiance;
translations.idiomatic: Let floating clouds be entirely cleared away and the bright sun increase in radiance;

sentences.zh: 道化侔羲、農，悠久配天地，實在此矣。

translations.literal: the Way and transformation match Fu Xi and Shen Nong, enduring and long matching Heaven and Earth—truly it lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: the Way and transformation match Fu Xi and Shen Nong, enduring and long matching Heaven and Earth—truly it lies in this.

sentences.zh: 伏以貞觀已來，左右起居有褚遂良、杜正倫、呂向、韋述等，鹹能竭其忠誠，悉心規諫。

translations.literal: This subject humbly notes that since the Zhenguan era, attendants of the left and right such as Chu Suiliang, Du Zhenglun, Lü Xiang, and Wei Shu all were able to exhaust their loyalty and sincerity and wholeheartedly remonstrate and advise.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly note that since the Zhenguan era, attendants of the left and right such as Chu Suiliang, Du Zhenglun, Lü Xiang, and Wei Shu all exhausted their loyalty and sincerity and wholeheartedly remonstrated and advised.

sentences.zh: 小臣謬參侍從，職奉起居，侍從之中，最近左右。

translations.literal: This petty official has wrongly joined the attendants; my duty is to serve at the imperial rising and resting; among attendants I am nearest to the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: I have wrongly joined the attendants; my duty is to serve at the imperial rising and resting; among attendants I am nearest to the left and right.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「近臣盡規。」

translations.literal: The Classic says, "Near ministers exhaust remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says, "Near ministers exhaust remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 則近侍之臣，上達忠款，實其本職也。

translations.literal: Then for near-attending ministers, conveying loyalty and sincerity upward is truly their basic duty.
translations.idiomatic: For near-attending ministers, conveying loyalty and sincerity upward is truly their basic duty.

sentences.zh: 疏奏忤旨，貶為江陵令。

translations.literal: The memorial offended the imperial intent and he was demoted to magistrate of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial offended the emperor and he was demoted to magistrate of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，柳泌等誅，征潾為兵部員外郎，遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Liu Bi and the others were executed; Lin was summoned as Vice Director in the Bureau of Military Appointments and transferred to Director in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Liu Bi and the others were executed; Lin was recalled as vice director in the Bureau of Military Appointments and promoted to director in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 有前率府倉曹曲元衡者，杖殺百姓柏公成母。

translations.literal: There was a former granary clerk of the Heir Apparent's guard, Qu Yuanheng, who beat to death the mother of the commoner Bai Gongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: A former granary clerk of the heir apparent's guard, Qu Yuanheng, had beaten to death the mother of a commoner named Bai Gongcheng.

sentences.zh: 法官以公成母死在辜外，元衡父任軍使，使以父廕征銅。

translations.literal: The judicial officers held that Gongcheng's mother died outside the term of offense; Yuanheng's father had served as military commissioner, so they had him pay a fine in copper by his father's hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: The judges held that the death fell outside the statutory term of offense and, because Yuanheng's father had been a military commissioner, fined him in copper under his father's hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 柏公成私受元衡資貨，母死不聞公府，法寺以經恩免罪。

translations.literal: Bai Gongcheng privately received goods and wealth from Yuanheng; his mother's death was not reported to the public offices; the Court of Justice, because grace had passed, remitted the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gongcheng had privately taken payment from Yuanheng and did not report his mother's death to the authorities; the Court of Justice, citing the recent amnesty, excused the crime.

sentences.zh: 潾議曰：「典刑者，公柄也。

translations.literal: Lin argued, saying: "Punitive law is the public handle.
translations.idiomatic: Lin argued: "Punishment is a public power of the state.

sentences.zh: 在官者得施於部屬之內；

translations.literal: One in office may apply it within subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: An official may apply it only within his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 若非在官，又非部屬，雖有私罪，必告於官。

translations.literal: If one is not in office and also not a subordinate, though there is a private offense, one must report to the office.
translations.idiomatic: If one is not in office and the victim is not a subordinate, even for a private offense one must report to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 官為之理，以明不得擅行鞭捶於齊人也。

translations.literal: The office judges it, to make clear that one may not on one's own authority wield the whip and cudgel against the people of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The office must judge it, to make clear that no one may freely beat the people.

sentences.zh: 且元衡身非在官，公成母非部屬，而擅憑威力，橫此殘虐，豈合拘於常典？

translations.literal: Moreover Yuanheng's person was not in office; Gongcheng's mother was not a subordinate—yet relying on power he wantonly committed this cruelty and violence; how can he be bound by the ordinary code?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng held no office, and Gongcheng's mother was not his subordinate—yet he abused his power with this cruelty; how can ordinary statutes apply?

sentences.zh: 柏公成取貨於讎，利母之死，悖逆天性，犯則必誅。」

translations.literal: Bai Gongcheng took goods from his enemy, profiting from his mother's death, rebelling against natural feeling—if he offends he must be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Bai Gongcheng took payment from his enemy and profited from his mother's death, defying natural feeling—if guilty, he must die."

sentences.zh: 奏下，元衡杖六十配流，公成以法論至死，公議稱之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was issued, Yuanheng was beaten sixty strokes and banished by assignment; Gongcheng was judged by law to death; public opinion praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was adopted, Yuanheng was beaten sixty strokes and exiled, and Gongcheng was sentenced to death by law; public opinion praised the outcome.

sentences.zh: 轉考功、吏部二郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the two directors in the Bureaus of Evaluations and Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director in the Bureaus of Evaluations and Appointments.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，拜給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoli he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoli he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，出為汝州刺史、兼御史中丞，賜紫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was sent out as prefect of Ruzhou, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and granted purple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he was sent out as prefect of Ruzhou and concurrent vice censor-in-chief and granted the purple robe.

sentences.zh: 坐違法杖殺人，貶左庶子，分司東都。

translations.literal: For unlawfully beating someone to death he was demoted to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent with detached assignment in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: For unlawfully beating a man to death he was demoted to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a detached post in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷左散騎常侍，充集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Left Attendant-in-Ordinary and appointed Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Left Attendant-in-Ordinary and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 集歷代文章續梁昭明太子《文選》，成三十卷，目曰《大和通選》，並音義、目錄一卷，上之。

translations.literal: He collected writings of successive ages continuing the Liang Crown Prince Zhaoming's 《Wenxuan》, completing thirty juan titled 《Comprehensive Selections of Taihe》, together with one juan of pronunciation and meaning and catalog, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled writings from successive dynasties as a continuation of the Liang Crown Prince Zhaoming's 《Wenxuan》, producing thirty juan titled 《Comprehensive Selections of Taihe》, with one juan of notes on pronunciation and a catalog, and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 當時文士，非素與潾遊者，其文章少在其選，時論鹹薄之。

translations.literal: Literary gentlemen of the time who had not been accustomed to associate with Lin had few of their writings in his selection; contemporary opinion all belittled it.
translations.idiomatic: Writers who had not been on familiar terms with Lin found few of their works included, and contemporary opinion widely disparaged the anthology.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉刑部侍郎，尋改華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments and soon changed to prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Vice Minister of Punishments and soon afterward was made prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，復拜刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was again appointed Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was again appointed Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，轉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng he was transferred to Vice Minister of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaicheng he was made Vice Minister of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 二年，加集賢院學士，判院事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was added as Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and oversaw academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and given charge of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋出為河南尹，入為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Metropolitan Governor of Henan and entered as Vice Minister of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as metropolitan governor of Henan, then recalled as Vice Minister of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 三年四月卒，贈戶部尚書，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he died; he was posthumously granted Minister of Revenue and given the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of the third year and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 潾以道義自處，事上盡心，尤嫉朋黨，故不為權幸所知。

translations.literal: Lin conducted himself by the Way and righteousness, served his superiors with full heart, and especially hated faction—therefore he was not known to the powerful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Lin lived by principle, served the throne wholeheartedly, and especially despised faction—so the powerful and favored did not know him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗竟以藥誤不壽，君子以潾為知言。

translations.literal: Xianzong in the end, through medicine's error, did not live long; gentlemen considered Lin one who knew how to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong ultimately shortened his life through elixirs, and gentlemen judged that Lin had spoken truly.

sentences.zh: 穆宗雖誅柳泌，既而自惑，左右近習，稍稍復進方士。

translations.literal: Though Muzong executed Liu Bi, afterward he himself became confused, and those close at hand and intimate attendants gradually again advanced wonder-workers.
translations.idiomatic: Though Muzong had Liu Bi executed, he soon fell under delusion again, and those around him gradually brought wonder-workers back to court.

sentences.zh: 時有處士張臯上疏曰：神慮淡則血氣和，嗜欲勝則疾疹作。

translations.literal: At that time the recluse Zhang Gao submitted a memorial, saying: When the spirit's thoughts are calm, blood and qi are harmonious; when desires prevail, illness and rash arise.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the recluse Zhang Gao submitted a memorial: When the spirit's thoughts are calm, blood and qi are harmonious; when desires prevail, illness and rash arise.

sentences.zh: 和則必臻於壽考，作則必致於傷殘。

translations.literal: When harmonious, one necessarily reaches longevity; when they arise, one necessarily comes to injury and disablement.
translations.idiomatic: When harmonious, one necessarily reaches longevity; when they arise, one necessarily comes to injury and disablement.

sentences.zh: 是以古之聖賢，務自頤養，不以外物撓耳目，不徇聲色敗性情。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages and worthies of antiquity strove to nourish themselves, not letting external things disturb eyes and ears, not indulging sound and color to ruin nature and feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sages and worthies of antiquity strove to nourish themselves, not letting external things disturb eyes and ears or indulging sound and color to ruin nature and feeling.

sentences.zh: 由是和平自臻，福慶斯集。

translations.literal: From this harmony and peace came of themselves, and blessings and felicity gathered.
translations.idiomatic: From this harmony and peace came of themselves, and blessings and felicity gathered.

sentences.zh: 故《易》曰：「無妄之疾，勿藥有喜。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Changes says, "Illness without cause—do not use medicine; there will be joy."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Changes says, "Illness without cause—do not use medicine; there will be joy."

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「自天降康，降福穰穰。」

translations.literal: The Odes says, "From Heaven comes peace; blessings descend abundantly."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, "From Heaven comes peace; blessings descend abundantly."

sentences.zh: 此皆理合天人，著在經訓。

translations.literal: These all accord in principle with Heaven and man and are set forth in the canonical teachings.
translations.idiomatic: These all accord in principle with Heaven and man and are set forth in the canonical teachings.

sentences.zh: 然則藥以攻疾，無疾固不可餌之也。

translations.literal: Thus medicines are used to attack illness; without illness one certainly must not ingest them.
translations.idiomatic: Thus medicines are used to attack illness; without illness one certainly must not ingest them.

sentences.zh: 高宗朝，處士孫思邈者，精識高道，深達攝生，所著《千金方》三十卷，行之於代。

translations.literal: In the reign of Gaozong, the recluse Sun Simiao had refined knowledge and lofty attainment of the Way, deeply understood nurturing life, and authored thirty juan of Prescriptions Worth a Thousand in Gold, which were practiced in the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Gaozong, the recluse Sun Simiao had refined knowledge and lofty attainment of the Way, deeply understood nurturing life, and authored thirty juan of Prescriptions Worth a Thousand in Gold, which were practiced in the age.

sentences.zh: 其《序論》云：「凡人無故不宜服藥，藥氣偏有所助，令人臟氣不平。」

translations.literal: Its Prefatory Discussion says, "Ordinary people should not take medicine without cause; the qi of medicine partially assists in one direction and makes a person's visceral qi unbalanced."
translations.idiomatic: Its Prefatory Discussion says, "Ordinary people should not take medicine without cause; the qi of medicine partially assists in one direction and makes a person's visceral qi unbalanced."

sentences.zh: 思邈此言，可謂洞於事理也。

translations.literal: Simiao's words here can be called penetrating in affairs and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Simiao's words here can be called penetrating in affairs and principle.

sentences.zh: 或寒暑為寇，節宣有乖，事資醫方，尚須重慎。

translations.literal: Sometimes cold and heat become invaders and seasonal regulation is at odds—then one relies on medical prescriptions, yet must still be heavily cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes cold and heat become invaders and seasonal regulation is at odds—then one relies on medical prescriptions, yet must still be heavily cautious.

sentences.zh: 故《禮》云：「醫不三代，不服其藥。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Rites says, "If the physician is not of three generations, do not take his medicine."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Rites says, "If the physician is not of three generations, do not take his medicine."

sentences.zh: 施於凡庶，猶且如此，況在天子，豈得自輕？

translations.literal: Applied to ordinary commoners, it is still like this—how much more for the Son of Heaven; how can one treat oneself lightly?
translations.idiomatic: Applied to ordinary commoners, it is still like this—how much more for the Son of Heaven; how can one treat oneself lightly?

sentences.zh: 先朝暮年，頗好方士，征集非一，嘗試亦多；

translations.literal: The previous dynasty in its later years greatly favored alchemical masters; summonses were not few, and trials were also many;
translations.idiomatic: The previous dynasty in its later years greatly favored alchemical masters; summonses were not few, and trials were also many;

sentences.zh: 果致危疾，聞於中外，足為殷鑒。

translations.literal: it truly brought on grave illness, heard within and without—enough to serve as a stern warning.
translations.idiomatic: it truly brought on grave illness, heard within and without—enough to serve as a stern warning.

sentences.zh: 皆陛下素所詳知，必不可更踵前車，自貽後悔。

translations.literal: All this Your Majesty has long known in detail; one certainly must not again follow the overturned cart and bring regret upon oneself.
translations.idiomatic: All this Your Majesty has long known in detail; one certainly must not again follow the overturned cart and bring regret upon oneself.

sentences.zh: 今朝野之人，紛紜竊議，直畏忤旨，莫敢獻言。

translations.literal: Now people at court and in the wilds murmur in private discussion, directly fearing to offend the imperial intent, and none dare offer words.
translations.idiomatic: Now people at court and in the wilds murmur in private discussion, directly fearing to offend the imperial intent, and none dare offer words.

sentences.zh: 臣蓬艾微生，麋鹿同處，既非邀寵，亦又何求？

translations.literal: This subject is a humble life among mugwort and artemisia, dwelling with deer; since I do not seek favor, what else do I seek?
translations.idiomatic: I am a humble life among mugwort and artemisia, dwelling with deer; since I do not seek favor, what else do I seek?

sentences.zh: 但泛覽古今，粗知忠義，有聞而默，於理不安。

translations.literal: But having broadly read antiquity and the present, I roughly know loyalty and righteousness; to hear and remain silent is unsettling in principle.
translations.idiomatic: But having broadly read antiquity and the present, I roughly know loyalty and righteousness; to hear and remain silent is unsettling in principle.

sentences.zh: 願陛下無怒芻蕘，庶裨萬一。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty not to be angry at this haycutter's counsel—perhaps it may help one part in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty not to be angry at this haycutter's counsel—perhaps it may help one part in ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 穆宗嘆獎其言，尋令訪臯，不獲。

translations.literal: Muzong sighed and praised his words, then ordered a search for Gao, but he was not found.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong sighed and praised his words, then ordered a search for Gao, but he could not be found.

sentences.zh: 李中敏，隴西人。

translations.literal: Li Zhongmin—Li Zhongmin was a man of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongmin was a native of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父嬰。

translations.literal: His father was Ying.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Ying.

sentences.zh: 中敏元和末登進士第，性剛褊敢言。

translations.literal: Zhongmin at the end of Yuanhe passed the jinshi; his nature was stern, narrow, and daring in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmin passed the jinshi late in Yuanhe; he was stern, uncompromising, and outspoken.

sentences.zh: 與進士杜牧、李甘相善，文章趣向，大率相類。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with jinshi Du Mu and Li Gan; their literary inclinations were in large measure alike.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to the jinshi Du Mu and Li Gan, and their literary tastes were much alike.

sentences.zh: 中敏累從府辟，入為監察，歷侍御史。

translations.literal: Zhongmin repeatedly followed regional staff recruitment, entered as investigating censor, and successively served as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmin served repeatedly on regional staffs, then entered court as investigating censor and rose to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為司門員外郎。

translations.literal: During Taihe he was Vice Director in the Bureau of Gatekeeping.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he was vice director in the Bureau of Gatekeeping.

sentences.zh: 六年夏旱，時王守澄方寵鄭註，及誣構宋申錫後，人側目畏之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year summer drought; at the time Wang Shoucheng was favoring Zheng Zhu, and after falsely framing Song Shenxi people looked askance and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year there was summer drought; Wang Shoucheng was then favoring Zheng Zhu, and after Zhu framed Song Shenxi people looked on him with fear.

sentences.zh: 上以久旱，詔求致雨之方。

translations.literal: Because of long drought the emperor ordered a search for methods to bring rain.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the prolonged drought the emperor ordered a search for means to bring rain.

sentences.zh: 中敏上言曰：「仍歲大旱，非聖德不至，直以宋申錫之冤濫，鄭註之奸弊。

translations.literal: Zhongmin submitted words, saying: "Year after year great drought is not because sage virtue has not arrived—it is directly because of the flood of injustice against Song Shenxi and the wicked abuses of Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmin wrote: "The drought year after year is not because Your Majesty's virtue has failed—it is directly because of the injustice done to Song Shenxi and the wickedness of Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 今致雨之方，莫若斬鄭註而雪申錫。」

translations.literal: Now the method to bring rain is none better than executing Zheng Zhu and clearing Shenxi's name."
translations.idiomatic: The surest way to bring rain is to execute Zheng Zhu and clear Song Shenxi's name."

sentences.zh: 士大夫皆危之，疏留中不下。

translations.literal: The scholar-officials all considered it perilous; the memorial was kept within and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were alarmed; the memorial was held within and never issued.

sentences.zh: 明年，中敏謝病歸洛陽。

translations.literal: The next year Zhongmin pleaded illness and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhongmin pleaded illness and retired to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及訓、註誅，竟雪申錫，召中敏為司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: When Xun and Zhu were executed, Shenxi's name was finally cleared; Zhongmin was summoned as Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit Records.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun and Zhu were executed and Shenxi's name was cleared, Zhongmin was recalled as vice director in the Bureau of Merit Records.

sentences.zh: 尋遷刑部郎中，知臺雜。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Punishments and oversaw censorate miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director in the Bureau of Punishments and given charge of censorate miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 其年，拜諫議大夫，充理匭使。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Remonstrance Grandee and served as commissioner for the Petition Box.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made Remonstrance Grandee and commissioner for the Petition Box.

sentences.zh: 上言曰：「據舊例，投匭進狀人先以副本呈匭使，或詭異難行者，不令進入。

translations.literal: He submitted words, saying: "According to old precedent, those who cast into the box and submit petitions first present a copy to the box commissioner; if strange or hard to carry out, they are not allowed to enter.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "By old precedent, petitioners first gave a copy to the box commissioner, who could block strange or difficult submissions from reaching the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣檢尋文按，不見本敕，所由但雲貞元奉宣，恐是一時之事。

translations.literal: Your servant searched the documents and precedents and does not see the original edict; those responsible only say it was announced in Zhenyuan—I fear it was a matter of one time.
translations.idiomatic: I have searched the records and find no original edict—officials cite only a Zhenyuan announcement, which may have been a temporary measure.

sentences.zh: 臣以為本置匭函，每日從內將出，日暮進入，意在使冤濫無告，有司不為申理者，或論時政，或陳利害；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the box was originally set up, brought out from within each day and entered at dusk, intending that those with flooded injustice and no one to tell, whom the offices do not judge for, might discuss current policy or set forth benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the box was meant to be brought out from the palace each morning and returned at dusk, so that those wronged with no recourse—when offices would not act—or who wished to discuss policy or report harm could reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 宜開其必達之路，所以廣聰明而慮幽枉也。

translations.literal: One should open the road by which they must reach—the means to broaden intelligence and consider hidden wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Their petitions should have a sure path to reach you—thus widening your awareness and reaching hidden wrongs.

sentences.zh: 若令有司先見，裁其可否，即非重密其事，俾壅塞自伸於九重之意。

translations.literal: If one lets the offices see first and judge whether it may proceed, that is not valuing secrecy of the matter and allowing obstruction of the intent that grievances reach the Ninefold Height by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If offices see petitions first and decide what may pass, that defeats the secrecy meant to let grievances reach the throne unblocked.

sentences.zh: 臣伏請今後所有進狀及封事，臣但為引進，取舍可否，斷自中旨。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly begs that hereafter for all submitted petitions and sealed matters, your servant only introduce them; acceptance or rejection, whether they may proceed, be decided by the central intent.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that hereafter I only introduce all petitions and sealed memorials, and that acceptance or rejection rest solely with Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 庶使名實在茲，以明置匭之本。」

translations.literal: Thus name and reality may rest here, to clarify the root purpose of setting up the box."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the institution's purpose may be honored and the reason for the box made clear."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 尋拜給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 李甘，字和鼎。

translations.literal: Li Gan—Li Gan, styled Heding.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan, whose courtesy name was Heding.

sentences.zh: 長慶末，進士擢第，又制策登科。

translations.literal: At the end of Changqing he passed the jinshi selection and also passed the policy-examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Changqing he passed the jinshi and also the policy examination.

sentences.zh: 太和中，累官至侍御史。

translations.literal: During Taihe he was repeatedly promoted to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he rose to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 鄭註入翰林侍講，舒元輿既作相，註亦求入中書。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu entered the Hanlin as lecture attendant; after Shu Yuanyu became chief minister, Zhu also sought entry into the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu entered the Hanlin as lecture attendant; after Shu Yuanyu became chief minister, Zhu also sought a post in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 甘唱於朝曰：「宰相者，代天理物，先德望而後文藝。

translations.literal: Gan proclaimed at court, saying: "The chief minister substitutes for Heaven in ordering things—first moral prestige, afterward literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Gan declared at court: "A chief minister stands in for Heaven to order the realm—moral stature must come before literary talent.

sentences.zh: 註乃何人，敢茲叨竊？

translations.literal: What sort of person is Zhu that he dares such brazen usurpation?
translations.idiomatic: Who is Zhu to dare such an appointment?

sentences.zh: 白麻若出，吾必壞之。」

translations.literal: If white hemp edict paper is issued, I will surely ruin it."
translations.idiomatic: If the appointment edict is issued, I will tear it apart."

sentences.zh: 會李訓亦惡註之所求，相註之事竟寢。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Xun also hated what Zhu sought, and the matter of making Zhu chief minister in the end was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun also opposed Zhu's bid, and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 訓不獲已，貶甘封州司馬。

translations.literal: Xun, having no other choice, demoted Gan to military adjutant of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to do otherwise, Xun demoted Gan to military adjutant of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 又有李款者，與中敏同時為侍御史。

translations.literal: There was also one Li Kuan, who at the same time as Zhongmin served as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Li Kuan, who served as attendant censor alongside Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 鄭註邠寧入朝，款伏閣彈註云：「內通敕使，外結朝官，兩地往來，卜射財貨。」

translations.literal: When Zheng Zhu of Binning entered court, Kuan lay prostrate at the gate and impeached Zhu, saying: "Within he communicates with edict commissioners; outside he binds with court officials; between the two places he goes back and forth, divining and shooting for goods and wealth."
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Zhu of Binning came to court, Kuan lay prostrate at the gate and impeached him: "He deals with edict commissioners inside the palace and binds with court officials outside, shuttling between them to extort wealth by divination."

sentences.zh: 文宗不之省。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 及註用事，款亦被逐。

translations.literal: When Zhu came to power, Kuan was also driven out.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu came to power, Kuan was driven out as well.

sentences.zh: 開成中，累官至諫議大夫，出為蘇州刺史，遷洪州刺史、江西觀察使。

translations.literal: During Kaicheng he was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Grandee, sent out as prefect of Suzhou, and transferred to prefect of Hongzhou and Jiangxi Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaicheng he rose to Remonstrance Grandee, then served as prefect of Suzhou and later as prefect of Hongzhou and Jiangxi observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 杜牧自有傳。

translations.literal: Du Mu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Du Mu has his own biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 高元裕，字景圭，渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Yuanyu—Gao Yuanyu, styled Jinggui, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanyu, whose courtesy name was Jinggui, was a native of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 祖甝。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Xing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Xing.

sentences.zh: 父集，官卑。

translations.literal: His father Ji held a low office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji held a low post.

sentences.zh: 元裕登進士第，本名允中，太和初，為侍御史，奏改元裕。

translations.literal: Yuanyu passed the jinshi; his original name was Yunzhong; at the beginning of Taihe he was attendant censor and memorialized to change his name to Yuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu passed the jinshi under the name Yunzhong; early in Taihe, as attendant censor, he memorialized to change his name to Yuanyu.

sentences.zh: 累遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔作相，用為諫議大夫，尋改中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Li Zongmin became chief minister he employed him as Remonstrance Grandee and soon changed him to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zongmin became chief minister he made Yuanyu Remonstrance Grandee and soon Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 九年，宗閔得罪南遷，元裕出城餞送，為李訓所怒，出為閬州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Zongmin offended and was transferred south; Yuanyu went outside the city to offer farewell gifts and was angered by Li Xun and sent out as prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Zongmin was disgraced and sent south, Yuanyu went out of the city to see him off; Li Xun was enraged and sent Yuanyu out as prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 時鄭註入翰林，元裕草註制辭，言註以醫藥奉召親，註怒。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Zhu entered the Hanlin; Yuanyu drafted Zhu's appointment text, saying Zhu was summoned by medicine to attend the kin—Zhu was angry.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Zhu entered the Hanlin, Yuanyu drafted his appointment text, noting that Zhu had been summoned for his medical skill—Zhu was furious.

sentences.zh: 會送宗閔，乃貶之。

translations.literal: Combined with seeing off Zongmin, he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Combined with his farewell to Zongmin, this led to his demotion.

sentences.zh: 訓、註既誅，復征為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After Xun and Zhu were executed he was again summoned as Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun and Zhu were executed he was recalled as Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，充翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng he served as Hanlin Lecture Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaicheng he became Hanlin lecture academician.

sentences.zh: 文宗寵莊恪太子，欲正人為師友。

translations.literal: Wenzong favored the Heir Apparent Zhuangke and wished upright men as teachers and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong favored Heir Apparent Zhuangke and wished upright men as his teachers and companions.

sentences.zh: 乃兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was then also made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu was also made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四年，改御史中丞，風望峻整。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to Vice Censor-in-Chief; his moral prestige was stern and ordered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became vice censor-in-chief, commanding stern respect.

sentences.zh: 上言曰：「御史府紀綱之地，官屬選用，宜得實才。

translations.literal: He submitted words, saying: "The Censorate is the place of law and discipline; in selecting officials one should obtain real talent.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The Censorate is the seat of discipline; its staff should be men of real ability.

sentences.zh: 其不稱者，臣請出之。」

translations.literal: Those who do not fit, your servant begs to remove."
translations.idiomatic: Those unfit for the post I ask permission to remove."

sentences.zh: 監察御史杜宣猷、柳壞、崔郢、侍御史魏中庸、高弘簡，並以不稱，出為府縣之職。

translations.literal: Investigating censors Du Xuanyou, Liu Huai, Cui Ying, attendant censors Wei Zhongyong and Gao Hongjian—all as unfit—were sent out to prefectural and county posts.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censors Du Xuanyou, Liu Huai, and Cui Ying and attendant censors Wei Zhongyong and Gao Hongjian were all removed as unfit and sent to prefectural and county posts.

sentences.zh: 尋而藍田縣人賀蘭，進與裏內五十余人相聚念佛，神策鎮將皆捕之，以為謀逆，當大辟。

translations.literal: Soon Helan Jin of Lantian County, together with more than fifty people in the lane gathering to chant Buddha's name, were all arrested by Divine Strategy garrison generals as plotting rebellion and sentenced to the great execution.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Helan Jin of Lantian County and more than fifty neighbors who had gathered to chant the Buddha's name were arrested by Divine Strategy garrison officers as rebels plotting treason and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 元裕疑其冤，上疏請出賀蘭進等付臺覆問，然後行刑，從之。

translations.literal: Yuanyu suspected their injustice and submitted a memorial requesting that Helan Jin and the others be handed to the Censorate for re-examination before carrying out punishment; the request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu suspected a miscarriage of justice and memorialized to have Helan Jin and the others remanded to the Censorate for re-examination before execution; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，為京兆尹。

translations.literal: During Huichang he was Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang he served as metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 大中初，為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong he was Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong he was Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 二年，檢校吏部尚書、襄州刺史，加銀青光祿大夫、渤海郡公、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was acting Minister of Civil Office Appointments and prefect of Xiangzhou, with addition of Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Duke of Bohai Commandery, and Shannan East Circuit Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was acting Minister of Civil Office Appointments and prefect of Xiangzhou, with the titles Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Duke of Bohai, and Shannan East Circuit military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，卒。

translations.literal: He entered as Minister of Civil Office Appointments and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Minister of Civil Office Appointments and died in office.

sentences.zh: 元裕兄少逸、元恭。

translations.literal: Yuanyu's elder brothers were Shaoyi and Yuangong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu's elder brothers were Shaoyi and Yuangong.

sentences.zh: 少逸，長慶末為侍御史，坐弟元裕貶官，左授贊善大夫，累遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: Shaoyi, at the end of Changqing was attendant censor; implicated by his younger brother Yuanyu's demotion, he was transferred left to Mentor of the Heir Apparent and repeatedly promoted to Director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi was attendant censor at the end of Changqing; implicated in his brother Yuanyu's demotion, he was demoted to Mentor of the Heir Apparent and later rose to director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元裕為中丞，少逸遷諫議大夫，代元裕為侍講學士。

translations.literal: When Yuanyu was vice censor-in-chief, Shaoyi was transferred to Remonstrance Grandee and replaced Yuanyu as lecture academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanyu became vice censor-in-chief, Shaoyi was made Remonstrance Grandee and replaced him as lecture academician.

sentences.zh: 兄弟叠處禁密，時人榮之。

translations.literal: The brothers layered in forbidden and secret posts; men of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers held successive posts in the inner palace, and contemporaries regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，為給事中，多所封奏。

translations.literal: During Huichang he was Attendant-in-Ordinary and many times sealed and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang he was Attendant-in-Ordinary and submitted many sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 大中初，檢校禮部尚書、華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong he was acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Huazhou, Tong Pass defense commissioner, and Zhenguo Army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong he was acting Minister of Rites, prefect of Huazhou, Tong Pass defense commissioner, and Zhenguo Army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為左散騎常侍、工部尚書，卒。

translations.literal: He entered as Left Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Public Works and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Left Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Public Works and died.

sentences.zh: 元裕子璩，登進士第。

translations.literal: Yuanyu's son Jun passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu's son Jun passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 大中朝，由內外制歷丞郎，判度支。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong court, from inner and outer edict drafter he passed through vice director posts and oversaw the Department of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong reign he rose from edict drafter through vice director posts to oversee the Department of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，守中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: During Xiantong he held Vice Director of the Secretariat and Participating Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiantong he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 李漢，字南紀，宗室淮陽王道明之後。

translations.literal: Li Han—Li Han, styled Nanji, was a descendant of the imperial clansman Prince Daoming of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, whose courtesy name was Nanji, was a descendant of Imperial Prince Daoming of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 道明生景融，景融生務該，務該生思，思生岌。

translations.literal: Daoming begot Jingrong, Jingrong begot Wugai, Wugai begot Si, Si begot Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming begot Jingrong, Jingrong begot Wugai, Wugai begot Si, and Si begot Ji.

sentences.zh: 岌已上無名位，及岌為蜀州晉原尉。

translations.literal: Above Ji there were no names or offices; when Ji was magistrate of Jinyuan in Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: None of Ji's forebears above him held office until Ji became magistrate of Jinyuan in Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 岌生荊，荊為陜州司馬。

translations.literal: Ji begot Jing; Jing was military adjutant of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji begot Jing, who served as military adjutant of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 荊生漢。

translations.literal: Jing begot Han.
translations.idiomatic: Jing begot Han.

sentences.zh: 漢，元和七年登進士第，累辟使府。

translations.literal: Han, in the seventh year of Yuanhe passed the jinshi and was repeatedly recruited to commissioner staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Han passed the jinshi in the seventh year of Yuanhe and served repeatedly on commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 長慶末，為左拾遺。

translations.literal: At the end of Changqing he was Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Changqing he was Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 敬宗好治宮室，波斯賈人李蘇沙獻沈香亭子材。

translations.literal: Jingzong loved constructing palaces; the Persian merchant Li Susa presented agarwood materials for a pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong loved building palaces; the Persian merchant Li Susa presented agarwood timber for a pavilion.

sentences.zh: 漢上疏論之曰：「若以沈香為亭子，即與瑤臺瓊室事同。」

translations.literal: Han submitted a memorial discussing it, saying: "If one uses agarwood for a pavilion, it is the same affair as jade towers and jasper chambers."
translations.idiomatic: Han memorialized: "To build a pavilion of agarwood is no different from the jade towers and jasper chambers of old."

sentences.zh: 寶歷中，王政日僻，漢與同列薛廷老，因入閣，廷奏曰：「近日除授不由中書，擬議多是宣出施行。

translations.literal: During Baoli, royal government daily grew perverse; Han and his colleague Xue Tinglao, on entering the inner court, Ting memorialized, saying: "Recently appointments and grants do not pass through the Secretariat; deliberation is mostly announced and issued for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoli, as governance grew ever more erratic, Han and his colleague Xue Tinglao entered the inner court; Ting memorialized: "Lately appointments have bypassed the Secretariat, with most orders issued directly from the palace.

sentences.zh: 臣恐自此紀綱大壞，奸邪恣行。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that from this discipline and law will greatly collapse and wicked men will act as they please.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that from this point discipline will collapse and the wicked will act at will.

sentences.zh: 願陛下各敕有司，稍存典故。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to charge each office and preserve somewhat the old precedents."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to charge each office to preserve the old precedents."

sentences.zh: 坐言忤旨，出為興元從事。

translations.literal: For words that offended the intent he was sent out as staff member in Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: For speaking against the emperor's wishes he was sent out as staff member in Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，召為屯田員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne he was summoned as Vice Director in the Bureau of State Farms and Historiographic Compiler in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended the throne he was recalled as vice director in the Bureau of State Farms and historiographic compiler.

sentences.zh: 漢，韓愈子婿，少師愈為文，長於古學，剛訐亦類愈。

translations.literal: Han was the son-in-law of Han Yu; the Junior Mentor Yu excelled in writing and was skilled in ancient learning; stern and censorious, he was also like Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Han was Han Yu's son-in-law; Yu excelled in letters and ancient learning, and Han's stern, censorious manner resembled his.

sentences.zh: 預修《憲宗實錄》，尤為李德裕所憎。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the 《Veritable Records of Xianzong》 and was especially hated by Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the 《Veritable Records of Xianzong》 and was especially disliked by Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，轉兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was transferred to Vice Director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he was made vice director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔作相，用為知制誥，尋遷駕部郎中。

translations.literal: When Li Zongmin became chief minister he employed him as Edict Drafter and soon transferred him to Director in the Bureau of Imperial Transport.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zongmin became chief minister he made Han edict drafter and soon director in the Bureau of Imperial Transport.

sentences.zh: 八年，代宇文鼎為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he replaced Yuwen Ding as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he replaced Yuwen Ding as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時李程為左僕射，以儀註不定，奏請定制。

translations.literal: At the time Li Cheng was Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; because ceremonial regulations were unsettled, he memorialized requesting fixed standards.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Cheng was Left Vice Director; because court ceremonial rules were unsettled, he memorialized to fix them.

sentences.zh: 先是，太和三年，兩省官同定左右僕射儀註：御史中丞已下，與僕射相遇，依令致敬，斂馬側立待。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the third year of Taihe, officials of the two departments together fixed ceremonial regulations for the Left and Right Vice Directors: from the Vice Censor-in-Chief downward, when meeting vice directors, according to ordinance they paid respects, reined in their horses and stood aside to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the third year of Taihe, officials of both departments had fixed the ceremonial rules for the vice directors: from the vice censor-in-chief down, when meeting a vice director one paid respects by reining in and standing aside.

sentences.zh: 僕射謝官日，大夫中丞、三院御史，就幕次參見，其觀象門外立班，既以後至為重。

translations.literal: On the day the vice director thanked for office, grandees, vice censors-in-chief, and censors of the three bureaus went to the tent side to pay respects; outside the Gate of Observing Phenomena they stood in ranks, esteem already resting on arriving later.
translations.idiomatic: On the day a vice director thanked for office, censorate grandees and the three bureaus' censors paid respects at the tent; outside the Gate of Observing Phenomena they stood in ranks, with later arrival counted as greater honor.

sentences.zh: 大夫中丞到班後，朝堂所由引僕射就位，傳呼贊導，始大夫就列之儀。

translations.literal: After grandees and vice censors arrived in ranks, court ushers led the vice director to position, called and guided praise, and only then did the grandee take rank in the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: After the censorate officers took their places, court ushers led the vice director in with announced guidance before the grandees assumed their ranks.

sentences.zh: 班退，贊導亦如之。

translations.literal: When ranks withdrew, praise and guidance were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When the ranks withdrew, the same procedure applied.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫與僕射道途相遇，則分道而行。

translations.literal: When the Censor-in-Chief and vice director met on the road, they took separate paths.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor-in-chief and a vice director met on the road, they took separate paths.

sentences.zh: 舊事，左右僕射初上，御史中丞、吏部侍郎已下羅拜。

translations.literal: By old practice, when the Left and Right Vice Directors first took office, the Vice Censor-in-Chief, Vice Minister of Civil Office Appointments, and those below bowed in rows.
translations.idiomatic: By old practice, when the Left and Right Vice Directors first took office, the vice censor-in-chief, Vice Minister of Civil Office Appointments, and those below bowed in rows.

sentences.zh: 四年，中書奏曰：「僕射受中丞侍郎拜，則似太重；

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Secretariat memorialized, saying: "If vice directors receive bows from vice censors and vice ministers, it seems too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Secretariat memorialized: "For vice directors to receive bows from vice censors and vice ministers seems too weighty a honor.

sentences.zh: 答郎官已下拜，則太輕。

translations.literal: To return bows to director-level officials and below is then too light.
translations.idiomatic: To return bows only to director-level officials and below would be too slight.

sentences.zh: 起今後，諸司四品已下官，及御史臺六品已下並郎官，並望準故事，余依元和七年敕處分。」

translations.literal: From now on, officials of the fourth rank and below in the various bureaus, and in the Censorate sixth rank and below together with director-level officials, all hope to follow old precedent; the rest follow the Yuanhe seventh-year edict disposition."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth officials of fourth rank and below in the ministries, and sixth rank and below in the Censorate together with director-level officials, should follow old precedent; the rest per the Yuanhe seventh-year edict."

sentences.zh: 可之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 至是，因李程奏，漢議曰：「左右僕射初上，受左右丞、諸曹侍郎、諸司四品及御史中丞已下拜。

translations.literal: At this time, because of Li Cheng's memorial, Han argued, saying: "When the Left and Right Vice Directors first take office, they receive bows from the Left and Right Assistants, bureau vice ministers, fourth-rank officials of the various bureaus, and the Vice Censor-in-Chief and below.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, responding to Li Cheng's memorial, Han argued: "When the Left and Right Vice Directors first take office, they receive bows from the Left and Right Assistants, bureau vice ministers, fourth-rank officials, and the vice censor-in-chief and below.

sentences.zh: 謹按《開元禮》及《六典》，並無此儀註，不知所起之由。

translations.literal: I respectfully examine the 《Kaiyuan Rites》 and the 《Six Canons》—none have this ceremonial regulation; I do not know the origin.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined the 《Kaiyuan Rites》 and the 《Six Canons》—neither records this ceremony, and I do not know when it began.

sentences.zh: 或以為僕射師長百僚，此語亦無證據，唯有曹魏時賈詡《讓官表》中一句語耳。

translations.literal: Some hold that vice directors are teachers and elders to the hundred officials—this saying also has no evidence; there is only one phrase in Jia Xu's Memorial Declining Office from Cao Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Some say vice directors are elders to all officials, but this has no support—only a single line in Jia Xu's Memorial Declining Office from Cao Wei.

sentences.zh: 且尚書令是正長，尚無受拜之文。

translations.literal: Moreover the Director of the Department of State Affairs is the true chief and still has no text of receiving bows.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Director of the Department of State Affairs is the true chief and has no provision for receiving bows.

sentences.zh: 故事，與御史中丞、司隸校尉，號三獨坐。

translations.literal: By old story, together with the Vice Censor-in-Chief and Colonel Director of Convicts they are called the Three Who Sit Alone.
translations.idiomatic: By tradition, together with the vice censor-in-chief and the colonel director of convicts they are called the Three Who Sit Alone.

sentences.zh: 伏以朝廷比肩，同事聖主，南面受拜，臣下何安？

translations.literal: I humbly consider that at court they stand shoulder to shoulder, serving the same sage lord—facing south and receiving bows, how can subordinates be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: At court they stand as equals serving the same sovereign—how can subordinates be at ease if one faces south to receive their bows?

sentences.zh: 縱有明文，尚須厘革。

translations.literal: Even if there is clear text, it still must be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Even if there is written authority, it should still be reformed.

sentences.zh: 故《禮記》曰：『君於士不答拜，非其臣則答之。』

translations.literal: Therefore the 《Book of Rites》 says: "The lord does not return bows to gentlemen; if not his minister, then he returns them."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Book of Rites》 says: "A lord does not return a gentleman's bow; if the man is not his minister, he may return it."

sentences.zh: 況御史中丞、殿中御史是供奉官，尤為不可。

translations.literal: Moreover the Vice Censor-in-Chief and Palace Censors are attendance officials—this is especially impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the vice censor-in-chief and palace censors are attendance officials—for them it is especially improper.

sentences.zh: 儀制令雖有隔品之文，不知便是受拜否？

translations.literal: Though the Ceremonial Code has text on separated ranks, I do not know whether this means receiving bows.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Ceremonial Code mentions separated ranks, it is unclear whether this means receiving bows.

sentences.zh: 及御史大夫，亦曾受御史已下拜，今並不行。

translations.literal: As for the Censor-in-Chief, he also once received bows from censors and below—now none of these are practiced.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief too once received bows from censors below him—now none of these are practiced.

sentences.zh: 蓋以禮數僭逼，非人臣所安。

translations.literal: Generally because ceremonial numbers overstep and press, it is not what human ministers can be at ease with.
translations.idiomatic: This is because such ceremonial excess is not what a subject can comfortably accept.

sentences.zh: 元和六年七月，詔崔邠、段平仲與當時禮官王涇、韋公肅等同議其事，理甚精詳。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yuanhe an edict ordered Cui Bin, Duan Pingzhong, and the ritual officials of the time Wang Jing and Wei Gongsu to deliberate together on the matter—the reasoning was very precise and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yuanhe sixth year the court ordered Cui Bin, Duan Pingzhong, and ritual officials Wang Jing and Wei Gongsu to deliberate—their reasoning was thorough.

sentences.zh: 今請舉而行之，庶為折衷。」

translations.literal: Now I beg to raise and carry it out, that it may serve as a balanced mean."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that their decision be adopted as the balanced standard."

sentences.zh: 時程入省，竟依舊儀，議者以漢奏為是。

translations.literal: At the time Cheng entered the Secretariat and in the end followed the old ceremony; discussants held Han's memorial correct.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng then entered the Secretariat and kept the old ceremony anyway; critics held that Han was right.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 八年。

translations.literal: The eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 改戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Civil Office Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year he became Vice Minister of Civil Office Appointments.

sentences.zh: 六月，李宗閔得罪罷相，漢坐其黨，出為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Li Zongmin offended and was removed as chief minister; Han sat in his faction and was sent out as prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Zongmin was disgraced and removed; implicated in his faction, Han was sent out as prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宗閔再貶，漢亦改汾州司馬，仍三二十年不得錄用。

translations.literal: When Zongmin was demoted again, Han was also changed to military adjutant of Fenzhou and for twenty or thirty years was not recorded for employment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongmin was demoted again, Han was reduced to military adjutant of Fenzhou and went twenty or thirty years without appointment.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，李德裕用事，漢竟淪躓而卒。

translations.literal: During Huichang Li Deyu held power; Han in the end fell into ruin and died.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang, when Li Deyu held power, Han fell into obscurity and died.

sentences.zh: 漢弟浐、洗、潘，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: Han's younger brothers Chan, Xi, and Pan all passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Han's younger brothers Chan, Xi, and Pan all passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 潘，大中初為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Pan, at the beginning of Dazhong was Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Pan served as Vice Minister of Rites early in Dazhong.

sentences.zh: 漢子貺，亦登進士第。

translations.literal: Han's son Kuang also passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Han's son Kuang also passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 李景儉，字寬中，漢中王瑀之孫。

translations.literal: Li Jingjian—Li Jingjian, styled Kuanzhong, was grandson of Prince Yu of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingjian, whose courtesy name was Kuanzhong, was grandson of Prince Yu of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 父褚，太子中舍。

translations.literal: His father Chu was Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chu was mentor of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 景儉，貞元十五年登進士第。

translations.literal: Jingjian, in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjian passed the jinshi in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 性俊朗，博聞強記，頗閱前史，詳其成敗。

translations.literal: His nature was handsome and bright; broadly informed with strong memory, he read much former history and knew its successes and failures in detail.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome and quick-witted, widely read with a strong memory, steeped in history and versed in its turns of fortune.

sentences.zh: 自負王霸之略，於士大夫間無所屈降。

translations.literal: He prided himself on kingly and hegemonic strategy and among scholar-officials bowed to none.
translations.idiomatic: He fancied himself a strategist in the mold of ancient kings and hegemons and deferred to no colleague.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，韋執誼、王叔文東宮用事，尤重之，待以管、葛之才。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan Wei Zhiyi and Wang Shuwen held power in the Eastern Palace and especially valued him, treating him with the talent of Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan, when Wei Zhiyi and Wang Shuwen ran the heir apparent's household, they prized him and treated him as a Guan Zhong or Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 叔文竊政，屬景儉居母喪，故不及從坐。

translations.literal: When Shuwen usurped government, it happened that Jingjian was in mourning for his mother, so he did not reach implicated punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen seized power, Jingjian was mourning his mother and thus escaped implication.

sentences.zh: 韋夏卿留守東都，辟為從事。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaqing remained to guard the Eastern Capital and recruited him as staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaqing, left to guard the Eastern Capital, recruited him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 竇君為御史中丞，引為監察御史。

translations.literal: Lord Dou became Vice Censor-in-Chief and brought him in as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou became vice censor-in-chief he brought Jingjian in as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 群以罪左遷，景儉坐貶江陵戶曹。

translations.literal: Qun was transferred left for crime; Jingjian sat in punishment and was demoted to revenue clerk of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Qun was demoted for his crimes, Jingjian was demoted to revenue clerk in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 累轉忠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually made prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 元和末入朝。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanhe he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 執政惡之，出為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: Those in power hated him and sent him out as prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The ruling faction disliked him and sent him out as prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 與元稹、李紳相善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Yuan Zhen and Li Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Yuan Zhen and Li Shen.

sentences.zh: 時紳、稹在翰林，屢言於上前。

translations.literal: At the time Shen and Zhen were in the Hanlin and repeatedly spoke of him before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Zhen were then in the Hanlin and spoke repeatedly of him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及延英辭日，景儉自陳己屈，穆宗憐之，追詔拜倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: On the day of farewell at the Yanchi audience, Jingjian himself stated he had been wronged; Muzong pitied him and by follow-up edict appointed him Vice Director in the Bureau of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: At his Yanchi farewell audience Jingjian pleaded that he had been wronged; Muzong took pity and recalled him as vice director in the Bureau of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 月余，驟遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month he was suddenly transferred to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he was abruptly made Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 性既矜誕，寵擢之後，淩蔑公卿大臣，使酒尤甚。

translations.literal: His nature being proud and extravagant, after favor and promotion he looked down on dukes, ministers, and great officials, and especially indulged in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and unrestrained by nature, after his rapid promotion he looked down on the highest officials and drank to excess.

sentences.zh: 中丞蕭俛、學士段文昌相交輔政，景儉輕之，形於談謔。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Xiao Xian and Academician Duan Wenchang alternated in assisting government; Jingjian slighted them and showed it in jest and mockery.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Xiao Xian and academician Duan Wenchang were alternating in power; Jingjian slighted them openly in jest.

sentences.zh: 二人俱訴之，穆宗不獲已，貶之。

translations.literal: Both complained; Muzong had no other choice and demoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Both complained to the emperor; unable to refuse, Muzong demoted him.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「諫議大夫李景儉，擢自宗枝，嘗探儒術，薦歷臺閣，亦分郡符。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Remonstrance Grandee Li Jingjian, promoted from the imperial branch, once explored Confucian arts, was recommended through the Censorate and Secretariat, and also shared prefectural seals.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Remonstrance Grandee Li Jingjian, raised from the imperial clan, once studied the classics, served in the Censorate and Secretariat, and held prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 動或違仁，行不由義。

translations.literal: In action he sometimes violated humaneness; in conduct he did not follow righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct often strayed from humaneness and did not follow righteousness.

sentences.zh: 附權幸以虧節，通奸黨之陰謀。

translations.literal: He attached to the powerful and favored to impair integrity and communicated with wicked factions' secret plots.
translations.idiomatic: He clung to the powerful at the cost of integrity and trafficked in factional intrigue.

sentences.zh: 眾情皆疑，群議難息。

translations.literal: All hearts were suspicious; collective opinion was hard to quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Public suspicion was widespread and criticism would not cease.

sentences.zh: 據因緣之狀，當置嚴科；

translations.literal: According to the circumstances of his connections, he should receive severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: By the evidence of his associations he deserved severe punishment;

sentences.zh: 順長養之時，特從寬典。

translations.literal: Following the season of nurturing growth, he is specially granted lenient statute.
translations.idiomatic: but in this season of nurturing growth he is granted leniency instead.

sentences.zh: 勉宜省過，無或徇非。

translations.literal: He is exhorted to examine and correct faults and not follow what is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Let him examine his faults and not persist in error.

sentences.zh: 可建州刺史。」

translations.literal: He may be prefect of Jianzhou."
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed prefect of Jianzhou."

sentences.zh: 未幾元稹用事，自郡召還，復為諫議大夫。
