translations.literal: Before long Yuan Zhen held power; from the prefecture he was summoned back and again made Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan Zhen came to power, recalled him from his prefecture, and restored him as Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，景儉朝退，與兵部郎中知制誥馮宿、庫部郎中知制誥楊嗣復、起居舍人溫造、司勛員外郎李肇、刑部員外郎王鎰等同謁史官獨孤朗，乃於史館飲酒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, after court Jingjian, together with Bureau of Military Appointments Director and Edict Drafter Feng Su, Bureau of the Treasury Director and Edict Drafter Yang Sifu, Diarist Wen Zao, Bureau of Merit Records Vice Director Li Zhao, and Bureau of Punishments Vice Director Wang Yi, alike visited Historiographer Dugu Lang and then drank wine in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: That twelfth month, after court Jingjian joined Military Appointments director and edict drafter Feng Su, Treasury director and edict drafter Yang Sifu, diarist Wen Zao, Merit Records vice director Li Zhao, and Punishments vice director Wang Yi in visiting historiographer Dugu Lang, and they drank in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 景儉乘醉詣中書謁宰相，呼王播、崔植、杜元穎名，面疏其失，辭頗悖慢。

translations.literal: Jingjian, riding his drunkenness, went to the Secretariat to visit the chief ministers, called out the names of Wang Bo, Cui Zhi, and Du Yuanying, and face to face set forth their faults—his words quite rebellious and disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Jingjian went to the Secretariat and confronted the chief ministers, naming Wang Bo, Cui Zhi, and Du Yuanying and rebuking their faults to their faces in insolent language.

sentences.zh: 宰相遜言止之，旋奏貶漳州刺史。

translations.literal: The chief ministers with yielding words stopped him and soon memorialized to demote him to prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers humored him into stopping and soon had him demoted to prefect of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是日同飲於史館者皆貶逐。

translations.literal: That day all who drank together in the History Office were demoted and driven out.
translations.idiomatic: That day all who had drunk in the History Office were demoted and banished.

sentences.zh: 景儉未至漳州而元稹作相，改授楚州刺史。

translations.literal: Before Jingjian reached Zhangzhou, Yuan Zhen became chief minister and changed his appointment to prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before Jingjian reached Zhangzhou, Yuan Zhen became chief minister and reassigned him to prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 議者以景儉使酒，淩忽宰臣，詔令才行，遽遷大郡。

translations.literal: Discussants held that Jingjian indulged wine, looked down on chief ministers, and the edict had barely been carried out when he was suddenly transferred to a great prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that Jingjian, drunk and insolent to the chief ministers, had barely been banished when he was suddenly given a major prefecture.

sentences.zh: 稹懼其物議，追還，授少府少監。

translations.literal: Zhen feared public criticism, recalled him, and appointed him Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing public criticism, Zhen recalled him and made him vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 從坐者皆召還。

translations.literal: Those implicated in sitting punishment were all summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Those punished with him were all recalled.

sentences.zh: 而景儉竟以忤物不得誌而卒。

translations.literal: Yet Jingjian in the end, because he offended others, did not realize his aims and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jingjian never achieved his ambitions, having offended too many, and died.

sentences.zh: 景儉疏財尚議，雖不厲名節，死之日，知名之士鹹惜之。

translations.literal: Jingjian was loose with wealth and valued debate; though he did not strictly uphold reputation and integrity, on the day of his death renowned gentlemen all regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjian was generous with money and loved debate; though not strict about reputation, noted men regretted his death.

sentences.zh: 景儉弟景儒、景信、景仁，皆有藝學，知名於時。

translations.literal: Jingjian's younger brothers Jingru, Jingxin, and Jingren all had artistic learning and were renowned in the time.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Jingru, Jingxin, and Jingren were all accomplished scholars renowned in their day.

sentences.zh: 景信、景仁，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: Jingxin and Jingren both passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxin and Jingren both passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 【贊】史臣曰：仲尼有言：「不得中行而與之，必也狂狷乎！」

translations.literal: [Praise] The historiographer says: Confucius had a saying: "If one cannot join with those of the middle way, one must have the impetuous and the narrow!"
translations.idiomatic: [Praise] The historiographer writes: Confucius said, "If one cannot keep company with those of the middle way, one must settle for the impetuous and the narrow!"

sentences.zh: 若渤論考第，仲方駁謚，誠知後悔，不能息言，可謂狷歟？

translations.literal: If Bo discussed evaluation ranks and Zhongfang rebutted the posthumous title—truly knowing regret yet unable to cease speaking—may this be called narrow?
translations.idiomatic: When Bo argued over evaluation ranks and Zhongfang rebutted a posthumous title—knowing regret yet unable to hold his tongue—was that not the narrow type?

sentences.zh: 當賊註挾邪之辰，群公結舌而寢默，而中敏、李甘、元裕，或肆其言，或奮其筆，暴揚醜跡，不憚撩須。

translations.literal: When the villain Zhu wielded wickedness, the host of lords bit their tongues and lay silent, yet Zhongmin, Li Gan, and Yuanyu—some unleashed their words, some exerted their pens, openly exposed ugly tracks, and did not fear ruffling beards.
translations.idiomatic: When the villain Zhu held sway, most officials held their tongues, yet Zhongmin, Li Gan, and Yuanyu—some with speech, some with the pen—exposed his foul deeds without fear of provoking his wrath.

sentences.zh: 謂之為狂，即有遺恨，比夫請劍斷佞，亦可同年而語也。

translations.literal: To call them impetuous yet leaves regret; compared with begging a sword to cut off the flatterer, they may also be spoken of in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: To call them merely impetuous is too slight; they may be compared with those who begged a sword to cut down a flatterer.

sentences.zh: 南紀有良史才，足以自立，而協比權幸，顛沛終身。

translations.literal: Nanji had talent for a good historian, enough to stand on his own, yet he joined with the powerful and favored and was tossed about his whole life.
translations.idiomatic: Nanji had the talent of a fine historian and could have stood on his own, yet he aligned with the powerful and spent his life in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 君子慎獨，庸可忽諸。

translations.literal: The gentleman is cautious in solitude—how can this be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman is cautious even in solitude—this cannot be neglected.

sentences.zh: 景儉自負太過，蕩而無檢，良驥中年跅弛之患也。

translations.literal: Jingjian prided himself too much, was dissolute without restraint—the affliction of a fine steed growing slack in mid-age.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjian thought too well of himself, was dissolute and unrestrained—the affliction of a fine horse going slack in midlife.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：張、李切言，利刃決云。

translations.literal: The praise says: Zhang and Li spoke cuttingly, like a sharp blade deciding clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Praise: Zhang and Li spoke with cutting force, like a sharp blade parting the clouds.

sentences.zh: 裴諫方士，深誠愛君。

translations.literal: Pei remonstrated against wonder-workers, with deep sincerity loving the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Pei remonstrated against wonder-workers out of deep loyalty to his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 言排賊註，高、李不群。

translations.literal: In speech they drove out the villain Zhu; Gao and Li did not flock with the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: They spoke against the villain Zhu; Gao and Li stood apart from the crowd.

sentences.zh: 漢、儉朋比，夫何足云。

translations.literal: Han and Jianian joined in faction—what is there worth speaking of?
translations.idiomatic: Han and Jianian clung to faction—what more need be said?
